How does a Dynamics 365 project run?

Every project runs the same four stages. You see the plan before enCloud9 builds, and every change after that is written down.

Stage APlanWe learn how you sell and serve, using a written discovery questionnaire, and give you the plan: apps, users, data, and where Copilot fits.
Stage BBuildWe build Dynamics 365 to the plan and move your data, then you check it before sign-off.
Stage CGo liveTraining, cut-over day, and Copilot and agents switched on where your data and permissions are ready.
Stage DRunYour support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed.

What does Dynamics 365 support cost?

Support plans start at $500 a month. After go-live, the people who built your system keep it running. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, and every monthly plan includes escalation to Microsoft when it is needed.

Book a call1-844-264-0729 →
How much does Dynamics 365 cost?

Microsoft list prices for Dynamics 365 Sales are $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly. Sales and Service Accelerators are $7,500, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each quoted in writing. Support starts at $500 a month. See our pricing guide.

How long does a Dynamics 365 setup take?

Our accelerators take 4 weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.

Can you take over a system another partner built?

Yes. Rescue and Repair is for Dynamics 365 systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date. We review it first and tell you what to keep.

Is Copilot included with Dynamics 365?

Copilot is built into Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise and Premium. Agents run on Copilot Credits, which most plans buy separately. We tell you what it costs to run before anything is switched on.

What is a generative page?

A page in your Dynamics 365 app that is built from a plain-words request, such as a report on deals that have gone quiet. It runs inside your Dynamics 365 app, on your live records.

A Dynamics 365 partner with one way of working

enCloud9 is a Microsoft Dynamics 365 partner for small and mid-sized businesses across the US. enCloud9 builds Dynamics 365, mostly Sales and Customer Service, and switches on Copilot where it helps. It connects the rest with Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI. enCloud9 also takes over failing Dynamics systems and gets them working again.

What do we believe about Dynamics 365 projects?

Nine plain rules we hold ourselves to on every project. If a line on this site breaks one of them, it should not be there.

  1. 01See the plan before we buildYou get the written plan: users, data, integrations and where Copilot fits, before any build work starts.

  4. 04Standard features firstWe build with standard features first, because over-customized systems are the ones we most often get called in to rescue.
  5. 05One process, every projectPlan, Build, Go live and Run, in that order, whatever the size of the project.
  6. 06Say what is included and what is notEvery package lists both. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.
  7. 07A number has a unit and a sourceIf we cannot show where a figure comes from, it does not go on the page.
  8. 08AI after a data and permissions reviewCopilot and agents go on top of a system that is ready, with the running cost written down first.

Home/Accessibility statement

Accessibility statement

Draft for Brian to approve. [Date published.]

We want everyone to be able to use encloud9.com, including people who use a screen reader, a keyboard, zoom or other assistive technology.

What standard do we work to?

We build this site to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA.

We test new pages before they go live and again when they change.

What do we check?

  • Automated accessibility tests on every page at phone and desktop widths.
  • Keyboard use: every link, button and menu can be reached and used without a mouse, and focus is visible.
  • Reduced motion: if your device asks for less motion, our animations stop.
  • Text and color contrast, headings in order, and labels on every form field.
  • Pages that work at 200% zoom without sideways scrolling.

Where might you still have trouble?

  • Some parts of the site come from other companies, such as our forms, the booking page and [the chat assistant]. We choose them with accessibility in mind, but we do not control all of their code.
  • Older blog posts and PDF guides may not meet the standard yet. We fix them as we update them.
  • [Known gaps found in testing, listed here with a date.]

How do I tell you about a problem?

Call us at 1-844-264-0729 or email sales@encloud9.com. Tell us the page and what got in the way. We reply within one business day.

When was this statement last reviewed?

[Date of last review.] We review it at least once a year and whenever the site changes in a big way.

Add-ons · Documents and e-signatures

Document Core Pack for Dynamics 365

Document Core Pack, made by mscrm-addons, creates quotes, contracts, reports and emails from your Dynamics 365 data using Word templates. It can send a document for e-signature through DocuSign or Adobe Sign and saves the signed copy back on the record. enCloud9 sets it up and builds your templates.

What does Document Core Pack do in Dynamics 365?

It turns records into finished documents without copying data into Word by hand. These are the jobs it does most often.

What Document Core Pack does, and where enCloud9 has built it
JobHow it worksWhere enCloud9 built it
Quotes from the CRMA Word template fills in from the quote, account and product records, then saves as a PDFMilestone Leasing: reps create standard quotes directly from Dynamics 365

When is Document Core Pack worth it?

When people copy CRM data into Word or Excel by hand, or chase signatures by email.

Book a call

A good fit if

  • Reps build quotes or proposals by copying CRM data into a Word file.
  • Contracts go out by email and come back signed in different places.
  • Reports are rebuilt by hand every month from the same records.
  • You send the same letter or document to many records at once.

Document Core Pack questions

Book a callAll questions →
What is Document Core Pack?

An add-on for Dynamics 365, made by mscrm-addons, that creates documents such as quotes, contracts and reports from your CRM data using Word templates.

Can Document Core Pack send documents for e-signature?

Yes. It works with DocuSign and Adobe Sign, among others. You can set one or more signers and the signing order, and the signed copy is saved back in Dynamics 365.

Which file types can it create?

PDF and Word documents, among other formats. Templates are built in Microsoft Word.

Can it run automatically?

Yes. It can create and send documents in batches, on a schedule, or from a Power Automate flow.

How much does Document Core Pack cost?

mscrm-addons publishes its prices by number of users, from $950 a year for up to 10 users. Every user who can edit records in Dynamics 365 needs a license. Our setup and template work is quoted after a short call.

Have you set it up for clients?

Yes. Milestone Leasing creates quotes with it, and PriceMDs uses it with Adobe Sign for e-signatures.

The short answerClickDimensions added dashboards inside Dynamics 365 for marketing results, starting with a Marketing Summary dashboard. They let teams see campaign, email, form, survey and landing page results without exporting data. New ClickDimensions Dashboards: Capabilities at a Glance

All dashboards are built right into Dynamics 365.

Where These Dashboards Actually Help

Most teams don’t struggle with access to data, they struggle with using it consistently.

Campaign Performance

Instead of reviewing campaigns one at a time, teams can quickly see how everything is performing in one place. This makes it easier to compare results and identify what’s working without building separate reports.

Email Performance

Email metrics are often reviewed after the fact. With dashboards, teams can spot issues like low engagement or high bounce rates earlier and make adjustments while campaigns are still active.

Forms and Conversions

Understanding why forms convert (or don’t) usually requires digging into details. These dashboards make that easier to see without pulling data into external tools.

Landing Page Performance

Instead of guessing which pages are working, teams can quickly identify which ones are actually driving leads and which need to be adjusted.

Home/Blog/Creating and Managing Sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales

Creating and Managing Sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales

Admin and how-to

By Kristin CanigliaJanuary 5, 2022Updated November 10, 20265 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedJanuary 5, 2022
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time5 minutes
  • Written byKristin Caniglia
On this page
  1. How do you create a new sequence?
  2. How do you connect a sequence to a record?
  3. How do you disconnect a sequence from a record?
  4. How do you edit a sales sequence?
  5. Is it easy to create and manage sequences?
  6. How do you get started with sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales?
  7. Which videos show how to use and modify sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales?
  8. Frequently asked questions
  9. Ready to set up sequences?

The short answerA sequence is a set of sales activities, such as emails, calls and tasks, that sellers follow in order. In Dynamics 365 Sales, you build sequences in the sales accelerator. Go to Sales Insights settings, select Sequences, then New sequence. Add your steps, save and activate. Then connect the sequence to records, such as leads or opportunities, by hand or with Power Automate.

Update, November 2026

What changed since this post was written?

This post is from January 2022. Every step below was checked against Microsoft Learn on 10 November 2026 and rewritten where the product has changed.

  • Microsoft now documents sequences as part of the sales accelerator in Dynamics 365 Sales. The settings area is still called Sales Insights settings.
  • A Sales Enterprise license includes the sales accelerator with 1,500 sequence-connected records a month. Sales Premium has no limit (Microsoft Learn, checked 10 November 2026).
  • New sequences can start from a template. Steps now include conditions, commands and LinkedIn activities.
  • You can connect a sequence four ways, and connect more than one sequence to a record.
  • You can edit an active sequence without deactivating it. Doing so creates a new version.

Sequences give sellers a set of steps that reflect the company’s best practices. Sales managers and admins create them, and sellers can create their own. They decide which activities sellers perform, and in what order.

That helps sellers prioritize their day, stay productive and follow the business process. When this post was written in 2022, sequences were a feature of Dynamics 365 Sales Insights. Today, Microsoft includes them in the sales accelerator (checked 10 November 2026).

How do you create a new sequence?

You create it in Sales Insights settings, under Sales accelerator. These are the current steps from Microsoft’s guide to creating and activating a sequence (checked 10 November 2026):

  1. Sign in to your sales app. In the lower-left corner, go to Change area and select Sales Insights settings.
  2. Under Sales accelerator, select Sequences.
  3. Select New sequence.
  4. Choose Use template or Use blank sequence.
  5. Enter a sequence name, an optional description and the entity. Lead is the default. You can also pick another record type set up for the sales accelerator, such as opportunity, account or contact.
  6. Select Next. The sequence designer opens with a Sequence start here step.
  7. Select the Add icon (+) to add each step. Step types are:
    • Steps: seller tasks such as an email, a phone call or a task
    • Conditions: the next action depends on whether a condition is met
    • Commands: the next action depends on a field value or a process stage
    • LinkedIn: social selling activities
  8. Space out steps with Set wait time. Do not end the sequence with a wait time, or activation can fail.
  9. Save the sequence.
  10. Select Activate, then Activate again to confirm.

Activating is the important last step. Only active sequences can be connected to records. An organization can have up to 250 active sequences at a time (checked 10 November 2026).

How do you connect a sequence to a record?

You connect it by hand or automatically. Once connected, the sequence’s activities show in order under Up next on the record. Microsoft’s page on connecting a sequence to records lists four ways (checked 10 November 2026). You can connect through the sequence, the record grid view, a single record, or Power Automate.

How do you connect a sequence to a record manually?

Start from the list of leads or opportunities:

  1. Go to Change area and select Sales.
  2. Select Leads or Opportunities.
  3. Select one or more records.
  4. Select Connect sequence on the command bar.
  5. Choose a sequence and select Connect.

You can also open a single record and select Connect sequence. Or open the sequence, go to its Connected leads tab and select Connect leads. A record can now have more than one sequence connected, for example one for the seller and one for the account manager.

How do you connect a sequence to a record automatically?

Use a Power Automate flow. The flow connects records to the sequence when its trigger meets the flow’s condition. In the flow, add the Microsoft Dataverse action Perform an unbound action and choose msdyn_ConnectSequence. Microsoft lists the fields to fill in under connecting a sequence through Power Automate (checked 10 November 2026).

How do you disconnect a sequence from a record?

Open the sequence’s connected records and select Disconnect. Microsoft’s training tutorial gives these steps (checked 10 November 2026):

  1. In Sales Insights settings, under Sales accelerator, select Sequences.
  2. Select More options next to the sequence, then View sequence.
  3. Select the Connected leads tab (or connected opportunities).
  4. Select the records to disconnect and select Disconnect.
  5. Confirm with Disconnect.

You can also open a connected record and select Disconnect sequence on the toolbar. Once disconnected, sellers no longer see that sequence’s steps on the record. In 2022 this was done from the sequence’s Properties. Today Properties shows the name, description, record type and owner (Microsoft Learn, checked 10 November 2026).

How do you edit a sales sequence?

Open the sequence and either deactivate it, copy it, or select Edit sequence. You need permission to edit sequences. By default, the System Administrator, Sequence manager, Sales Manager and Salesperson roles have it (Microsoft Learn, checked 10 November 2026).

In 2022 you had to deactivate a sequence before editing it. Microsoft’s guide to cloning and editing a sequence now gives three choices (checked 10 November 2026):

  • Deactivate it, edit, then activate it again.
  • Create a copy, edit the copy, then activate it.
  • Edit sequence on an active sequence. This creates a new version. Records already connected stay on the old version (checked 10 November 2026).

To add a step, use the Add icon as you did when creating it. To change a step, select it, edit the details in the right pane and select Save. To remove a sequence for good, see Microsoft’s steps to delete a sequence (checked 10 November 2026).

Is it easy to create and manage sequences?

Yes. Once the sales accelerator is set up, creating and managing sequences is straightforward. Sequences help sellers prioritize activities, stay productive and follow your business process.

How do you get started with sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Check your license, then set up the sales accelerator. A Sales Enterprise license includes 1,500 sequence-connected records a month. Sales Premium removes that limit (checked 10 November 2026).

Prices have changed since this post first ran in 2022. See enCloud9’s Dynamics 365 pricing page for today’s figures.

enCloud9 has been a Microsoft Partner since 2008. Its Sales Accelerator package sets up Dynamics 365 Sales for your pipeline for $7,500. Contact enCloud9 for help setting up sequences.

Which videos show how to use and modify sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Two short enCloud9 videos walk through it:

  • How to Modify Sequences in Dynamics 365 (enCloud9 on YouTube): duplicating, editing and improving sequences.
  • Using Sequences in Dynamics 365 Sales (enCloud9 on YouTube): creating and applying sequences for consistent follow-up.

Both videos predate this update, so some screens may look different today.

Frequently asked questions

What is a sequence in Dynamics 365 Sales?

A set of sales activities, such as emails, calls and tasks, that sellers follow in order. Managers, and sellers for themselves, build sequences in the sales accelerator and connect them to records such as leads or opportunities.

Do I need Sales Premium to use sequences?

No. A Sales Enterprise license includes the sales accelerator with 1,500 sequence-connected records a month. Sales Premium has no monthly limit.

Can I edit a sequence that is already active?

Yes. Select Edit sequence to create a new version. Records already connected stay on the old version. You can also deactivate the sequence or edit a copy.

Why Your Dynamics 365 CRM Feels Like Extra Work Instead of a Helpful Tool

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyJuly 17, 2026Updated November 10, 20264 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedJuly 17, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. Why does Dynamics 365 start to feel like extra work?
  2. What is the difference between a system of record and a system of engagement?
  3. How do you know Dynamics 365 no longer drives the work?
  4. Why does it matter if people work outside the CRM?
  5. How do you turn Dynamics 365 back into a system of engagement?
  6. How can enCloud9 help with Dynamics 365 adoption?
  7. Frequently asked questions
  8. Ready to make Dynamics 365 more useful?

The short answerDynamics 365 starts to feel like extra work because of friction, not user resistance or a lack of training. Too many required fields, hard-to-find information, unclear sales stages and duplicate entry push work into Outlook, Teams and spreadsheets. The fix is to make the CRM the easiest place to find information, set priorities and move customer work forward.

When most organizations implement Dynamics 365, the goal is clear. They want efficiency, visibility into customer relationships, and a single source of truth for sales and service data.

Early on, it works. Salespeople check the CRM before calls. Service teams review account history. Managers use dashboards. The CRM is where work happens.

Over time, something changes. Users keep logging in, but the system starts to feel like extra work. Adoption stalls.

Why does Dynamics 365 start to feel like extra work?

The cause is usually friction, not users resisting change or a lack of training. Friction shows up in small ways:

  • Forms with too many required fields
  • Important information that is hard to find
  • Sales stages nobody can define clearly
  • The same information entered more than once
  • Record updates that take too long

So conversations move to Outlook, Teams, spreadsheets or personal notes. The CRM gets updated later, if at all. It becomes a place to document work after the fact, instead of the place where work begins.

What is the difference between a system of record and a system of engagement?

A system of record tells you what happened. A system of engagement helps you decide what to do next.

Dynamics 365 is a system of record. It keeps customer data, opportunities, activities and service history in one place. Its greatest value comes when it also works as a system of engagement, one that helps people take action.

When the CRM stops helping people move work forward, users keep entering data. They just stop relying on it.

How do you know Dynamics 365 no longer drives the work?

Ask one question: when employees need customer information, is Dynamics 365 the first place they look?

Login counts, activity records and opportunity updates are useful. They don’t tell the full story. If people do not check Dynamics 365 first, adoption is probably weaker than your reports suggest. Watch for these warning signs:

  • Employees ask coworkers for updates before they check the CRM.
  • Customer notes go in days after the meeting or call.
  • Opportunities get updated only before pipeline reviews.
  • Teams keep spreadsheets outside the CRM.
  • People ask questions the customer record should already answer.
  • Users see the CRM as an admin chore, not a useful tool.

Behind each sign is the same problem. Users no longer trust the CRM, depend on it or see value in it.

Why does it matter if people work outside the CRM?

Work done outside the CRM splits customer information across places, and everything built on that information gets weaker.

  • Reports become less reliable.
  • Managers see less of what is happening.
  • People lose time searching for data.

Copilot and other AI tools need complete, accurate and current data. Information kept in spreadsheets, email or personal notes weakens what those tools can tell you.

The more people rely on the CRM every day, the more value you get from it. The same goes for the tools built on top of it.

How do you turn Dynamics 365 back into a system of engagement?

Make the CRM useful rather than mandatory, one role at a time.

  • Salespeople: quick access to customer history, upcoming activities, open opportunities and next steps.
  • Service representatives: account details, past interactions and case history the moment they need them.
  • Managers: CRM data in meetings, instead of separate spreadsheets.

The goal isn’t more time in the system. It is making the CRM the easiest place to find information, set priorities and move customer relationships forward. When that happens, adoption improves on its own.

How can enCloud9 help with Dynamics 365 adoption?

enCloud9 works with organizations that already have Dynamics 365 but aren’t getting the value they expected. Usually the cause is friction and a poor user experience. enCloud9 helps you:

  • Simplify forms and improve usability
  • Cut unnecessary data entry
  • Streamline sales and service processes
  • Improve user adoption and engagement
  • Set up dashboards and views for daily work
  • Find workflow bottlenecks and friction points
  • Prepare Dynamics 365 for Copilot and AI

enCloud9 treats Dynamics 365 optimization as ongoing work, not a one-time project. Read enCloud9’s client stories to see what that looks like.

Further reading on the enCloud9 blog:

  • Why Dynamics 365 adoption breaks, and why more training won’t fix it
  • Dynamics 365 optimization: how to fix what’s slowing your system down
  • The hidden cost of an overbuilt Dynamics 365 CRM

Frequently asked questions

Is low Dynamics 365 adoption a training problem?

Usually not. The usual cause is friction: too many required fields, hard-to-find information, unclear stages, duplicate entry and slow updates. More training does not remove any of those.

How do you measure Dynamics 365 adoption?

Login counts and activity records help, but they miss the main question. When people need customer information, is Dynamics 365 the first place they look?

Does low adoption affect Copilot?

Yes. Copilot and other AI tools need complete, accurate and current data. Information kept in spreadsheets, email or personal notes weakens what they can tell you.

About the author: Brian Begley

Brian Begley is the founder and CEO of enCloud9.

Ready to make Dynamics 365 more useful?

If your team logs in to Dynamics 365 but still relies on Outlook, Teams, spreadsheets or coworkers, the CRM has drifted. That can be reversed. An optimization review finds the friction and shows why people work outside the system. It helps make Dynamics 365 a tool for getting work done, not just for reporting.

Dynamics 365 Pricing and Licensing: The 2026 Guide

Refresh of the 2025 guide Pricing and licensing · Dynamics 365

By Brian BegleyPublished June 18, 2025Updated November 10, 20267 min readPrices checked on Microsoft's pages, 4 Nov 2026

At a glance

  • Sales$65 to $150
  • Customer Service$50 to $195
  • Monthly billing5% more than yearly
  • Copilot Credit pack$200 for 25,000
On this page
  1. How much does each Dynamics 365 app cost in 2026?
  2. How does Dynamics 365 licensing work?
  3. What do Copilot and agents cost in 2026?
  4. What drives your total cost?
  5. How do you pick the right Dynamics 365 license?
  6. Frequently asked questions
  7. Are you paying for the right licenses?

The short answerIn 2026, Dynamics 365 Sales costs $65 to $150 per user per month, Customer Service costs $50 to $195, Field Service costs $105 and Project Operations costs $135. These are Microsoft list prices, paid yearly. Paying monthly on an annual plan costs 5% more. Copilot agents run on Copilot Credits, which most plans buy separately.

Prices checked 4 November 2026. All prices are Microsoft US list prices in US dollars, per user per month, paid yearly, unless a row says otherwise. Microsoft changes prices, and your price can differ by country, currency and agreement. Confirm current pricing before you buy.

How much does each Dynamics 365 app cost in 2026?

Dynamics 365 Sales

Dynamics 365 Sales plans
PlanPriceBest for
Sales Professional$65Small sales teams that need core pipeline tracking
Sales Enterprise$105Most B2B sales teams; includes Copilot in Sales, Outlook and Teams
Sales Premium$150Teams that want 1,000 Copilot Credits per user per month for agents
Microsoft Relationship SalesNot listed; ask Microsoft or a partnerSales Enterprise plus LinkedIn Sales Navigator; 10-seat minimum

Source: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales pricing, checked 4 November 2026.

Customer Service and Contact Center

Customer Service and Contact Center plans
PlanPriceBest for
Customer Service Professional$50Basic case management
Customer Service Enterprise$105Full case management, queues, knowledge and service levels
Customer Service Premium$195Case work and contact center in one plan, with Copilot Credits included
Contact Center$110Voice and digital channels together
Contact Center Digital$95Chat and messaging only
Contact Center Voice$95Phone only

Source: Microsoft Customer Service pricing; Microsoft Contact Center pricing, checked 4 November 2026.

Microsoft notes that Contact Center has discount pricing when bought with Customer Service Enterprise. Voice calling runs on Azure Communication Services, which is billed separately.

Field Service and Project Operations

Field Service and Project Operations plans
PlanPriceBilling basis
Field Service$105Per user per month, paid yearly
Field Service Contractor$50Per user per month, paid yearly
Resource Scheduling Optimization add-in$30Per resource per month, paid yearly
Project Operations$135Per user per month, paid yearly

Source: Microsoft Field Service pricing; Microsoft Project Operations pricing, checked 4 November 2026.

Customer Insights

Customer Insights is priced per company (tenant), not per user. Users are unlimited.

Customer Insights plans
PlanPrice per company per monthIncludes
Customer Insights$1,700100,000 unified people and 10,000 interacted people
Customer Insights Attach$1,000Same entitlements; needs 10 or more users of a qualifying Dynamics 365 app

Source: Microsoft Customer Insights pricing, checked 4 November 2026.

Team Members

Team Members is a low-cost license for people who mostly read data and do light tasks, like entering time or updating a record they own. Microsoft does not show its price on its public Dynamics 365 pricing pages. Ask your partner or check the Microsoft 365 admin center for the current figure.

How does Dynamics 365 licensing work?

  • One base license per user. Each full user gets one base license, for the highest-priced app that user needs.
  • Attach licenses for more apps. If the same person needs a second app, you add an attach license at a lower price instead of a second full license. A sales manager on Sales Enterprise who also works service cases gets Sales Enterprise as the base and a Customer Service attach license.
  • Team Members for light users. Staff who only view records, enter time or update a few items can use Team Members. Team Members covers Microsoft’s set Team Member apps, which can be customized with up to 15 extra tables. Custom apps need a full license (see Microsoft’s licensing guidance). If a Team Members user starts doing full work, Microsoft expects a full license.
  • Minimums. Most apps have no minimum user count. Microsoft Relationship Sales needs 10 seats, and Customer Insights Attach needs 10 or more users of a qualifying app.
  • Yearly or monthly. Since 1 April 2025, monthly billing on an annual subscription costs 5% more than paying up front.
  • Where to buy. From Microsoft directly, through the Microsoft 365 admin center, or through a Microsoft Partner.

More on base, attach and Team Members on our Dynamics 365 licensing page.

What do Copilot and agents cost in 2026?

There are three different AI costs to budget for.

1. Copilot built into Dynamics 365. Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium include Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams at no extra cost. Sales Professional does not. Contact Center plans include Copilot in the service rep desktop, such as case summaries, email help and knowledge answers.

2. Agents and Copilot Credits. Agents do work on their own, such as qualifying leads or researching accounts. Running agents uses Copilot Credits. Sales Premium includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user per month, pooled across your company, and Customer Service Premium also includes credit capacity. Other plans buy credits:

Copilot Credit options
OptionPriceHow it bills
Copilot Credit pack$200 per pack per month25,000 credits per pack, company-wide, paid up front
Pay-as-you-goRate per credit not shown on Microsoft's pricing pageBilled monthly through an Azure subscription
Pre-purchase planSavings shown on Microsoft's pre-purchase pageOne-year commitment, then pay-as-you-go when used up

Source: Microsoft Copilot Studio pricing, checked 4 November 2026.

How many credits you use depends on the agent. Microsoft's rates include 2 credits for a generative answer, 5 credits for an agent action and 10 credits for tenant graph grounding. One question can use several of these at once.

3. Microsoft 365 Copilot. A separate add-on for Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams: [price re-read on Microsoft's page at launch]. Microsoft 365 Copilot Business, for up to 300 users, lists at $21 per user per month; a 15% promotion brings it to $18 on an annual subscription through 31 December 2026. It needs a Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard or Premium license. Agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot carry no extra credit charge for users who have that license. More on our Copilot and AI page.

What drives your total cost?

Licenses are only part of the bill.

  • Licenses. Users times price, paid yearly. 10 Sales Enterprise users cost 10 x $105 = $1,050 per month, or $12,600 per year at list price. Paid monthly, the same seats cost about 5% more.
  • Storage. Every company gets a default amount of Dataverse storage, and full user licenses add more. Extra database storage is $40 per GB per month, paid yearly. Once a company passes 100% of its storage, creating, copying and restoring environments is blocked. Microsoft is rolling out stricter checks: once they reach your tenant, sandboxes go to admin-only mode after 30 days and sign-in to them is blocked after 90 days. Production environments keep running (Microsoft’s capacity rules). See Dataverse storage.
  • Copilot Credits if you plan to run agents, unless you are on a Premium plan with credits included.
  • Implementation and support. Setup, data moves, integrations and training depend on your scope. After go-live, you need someone to keep the system healthy.
enCloud9 support plans, 12-month agreement
PlanPriceHours included
On-Demand$200 per hourPay as you go
Stability$500 per month4 hours per month
Optimization$1,500 per month20 hours per month
PartnershipFrom $2,000 per month35 hours per month

Stability, 4 hours a month, is the minimum plan for new clients. So a 10-user Sales Enterprise team with the Stability plan starts at about $1,550 per month before any implementation project or Copilot Credits. See support plans.

How do you pick the right Dynamics 365 license?

  • Sales team: start with Sales Enterprise. Choose Professional only if you do not need Copilot or advanced forecasting. Choose Premium if you plan to run agents at volume, since the included credits may cover what you would buy anyway.
  • Service team: start with Customer Service Enterprise. Add Contact Center if you take calls or chats in Dynamics 365. Look at Customer Service Premium if you need both.
  • Field team: Field Service for technicians and dispatchers, Field Service Contractor for outside contractors.
  • Project business: Project Operations for project managers; Team Members for staff who only enter time and expenses.

Two common ways to overpay: full licenses for people who only need Team Members, and two full licenses where one base plus an attach would do.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Dynamics 365 cost per user?

At Microsoft list price, paid yearly, Dynamics 365 Sales runs $65 to $150 per user per month, Customer Service $50 to $195, Field Service $105 and Project Operations $135. Customer Insights is priced per company, starting at $1,000 per month with attach pricing.

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365?

Partly. Sales Enterprise and Premium include Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams. Running agents uses Copilot Credits. Sales Premium includes 1,000 credits per user per month; other plans buy credits from $200 per 25,000-credit pack per month or pay as they go.

What is the cheapest Dynamics 365 license?

For full users, Customer Service Professional and Field Service Contractor are the lowest listed prices at $50 per user per month. For light users, the Team Members license costs less; ask your partner for the current price.

What is a Dynamics 365 attach license?

An attach license adds a second app to a user who already has a base license, at a lower price than a full license. The base must be the highest-priced app that user needs.

Can I pay for Dynamics 365 monthly?

Yes. Microsoft's listed prices are for paying yearly. Paying monthly on an annual subscription costs 5% more, a rule Microsoft has applied since 1 April 2025.

Is there a minimum number of users for Dynamics 365?

Most apps have no minimum on Microsoft's pricing pages. Microsoft Relationship Sales needs 10 seats, and Customer Insights Attach needs 10 or more users of a qualifying Dynamics 365 app.

Did Dynamics 365 prices go up in 2026?

Microsoft's Dynamics 365 pricing pages show no dated 2026 list price change for these apps. The bigger changes are about AI and storage: Premium plans include Copilot Credits, agents are part of the Sales plans, and storage overage rules are stricter. Microsoft 365 suite prices rose on 1 July 2026.

About the author: Brian Begley

Brian Begley is the founder and CEO of enCloud9. enCloud9 checks every Microsoft price in this guide on Microsoft's own pages before it goes live.

Smarter Selling with the Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent

Copilot and AI

By Brian BegleyAugust 18, 2025Updated November 10, 20263 min read

On this page
  1. What changed since 2025?
  2. What Is the Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent?
  3. How does the agent handle a new lead?
  4. Why use the Sales Qualification Agent?
  5. How do you get started with the Sales Qualification Agent?
  6. Final Thoughts
  7. Partner with Dynamics 365 Sales Experts at enCloud9
  8. Want help with this?

The short answerThe Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent is an AI agent inside Dynamics 365 Sales that researches and scores each new lead against your ideal customer profile, using Microsoft’s FIRE model: Fit, Intent, Recency and Engagement. In research-only mode it enriches and scores leads; in research and engage mode it also emails prospects and hands good leads to sellers.

Update, November 2026

What changed since 2025?

The Sales Qualification Agent is no longer marked preview on Microsoft Learn. It runs on Copilot Credits, prepaid or pay-as-you-go.

The original 2025 post follows.

Qualifying leads takes time, and often, that time goes to waste when those leads don’t convert. To address this challenge, Microsoft introduced the Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent, a powerful AI tool built into Dynamics 365 Sales.

This feature helps sales teams focus their time on leads that are most likely to close.

What Is the Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent?

The Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent is an AI assistant that works inside Dynamics 365 Sales. It handles lead research, scoring, and, in its full version, email outreach and follow-up. The agent checks each new lead against your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). If the lead is a good match, it moves forward in the process.

This tool runs in two different modes:

  • Research-only: It enriches lead details, scores them for fit, and shares the data with your team.
  • Research & Engage: It also sends custom emails, follows up, reads responses, and sends good leads to sellers.

The agent uses Microsoft’s FIRE model, Fit, Intent, Recency, and Engagement, to qualify leads in a consistent and intelligent way. For a deeper look, check out this Microsoft Learn article.

How does the agent handle a new lead?

It researches the lead, scores it against your ideal customer profile, and either sets it aside or reaches out, as in this made-up scenario.

Suppose you sell software to mid-sized manufacturers.

One day, a person named Paul fills out your contact form using a Gmail address. The agent checks the info, marks the email as invalid, and deprioritizes the lead. No action is needed from your team.

Later that same day, Sarah, a sales director at a large manufacturer, fills out the same form. She uses a valid business email and matches your ICP. The Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent sends her a custom email. She clicks a link to learn more. Based on that engagement, the agent qualifies the lead and hands it off to your rep.

In this case, the agent saved time, avoided bad data, and passed a warm lead to your sales team, all automatically.

Why use the Sales Qualification Agent?

It lets reps spend time selling instead of digging through cold leads. That’s exactly what this feature helps with.

It gives your team a better way to manage the top of your funnel by:

  • Saving time: Reps focus only on qualified leads.
  • Improving quality: The agent filters out bad data and low-fit contacts.
  • Speeding up follow-up: Prospects can get an email within seconds.
  • Creating consistency: Every lead is reviewed using the same criteria.

Even if you’re already using automation, the Dynamics 365 Sales Agent adds AI-powered insight to help your team prioritize faster and smarter.

How do you get started with the Sales Qualification Agent?

Check that your environment meets Microsoft’s requirements: mailbox setup, server-side sync and licensing. If it’s not showing up yet, it could be due to your region or version.

To start using the Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent, make sure your system meets the technical requirements. These include mailbox setup, server-side sync, and licensing. Microsoft outlines everything you need in its step-by-step guide.

Final Thoughts

It helps your team move faster, work smarter, and stay focused on real opportunities. Instead of wasting time on unqualified leads, your team can spend more time closing deals.

Now’s the time to test it, adjust your ICP, and bring smarter selling into your business.

Generative pages in Dynamics 365: what they are and 12 ways to use them

Draft for the December theme Copilot and AI · Generative pages

By [Author][Publish date]5 min readFacts checked on Microsoft Learn, 5 Nov 2026

Book a call

At a glance

  • Status, November 2026Generally available
  • Data per pageUp to six Dataverse tables
  • Cost to buildNo extra AI or message credits
  • Ways to buildIn the browser or with an AI coding tool
On this page
  1. What is a generative page?
  2. How do you build one?
  3. Where do generative pages show up?
  4. What are 12 ways to use generative pages?
  5. When should you not use a generative page?
  6. What do you need to get started?
  7. What is the status and licensing (November 2026)?
  8. Frequently asked questions
  9. Want to see what one could do for your team?

The short answerGenerative pages let you describe a screen in plain English and get a working page inside a Dynamics 365 app. Microsoft's app agent writes the code and connects it to your Dataverse tables, and you refine it by chatting. They are generally available and fit best when a team needs one focused screen that standard views lack.

What is a generative page?

Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service, Field Service and Project Operations run as model-driven apps in Power Apps. A generative page is a new kind of page you can add to those apps.

You describe the page you want. You pick the tables it should use. You can even attach a sketch of the layout. Microsoft's app agent then plans the page, writes React code, and shows you a live preview. If something is off, you tell it what to change, or you edit the code yourself.

The AI does its work while the page is being built. The finished page is an ordinary screen that reads and updates your Dynamics 365 records, and we test it with your users' real security roles before anyone relies on it.

How do you build one?

There are two ways.

Way 1

In the browser. In Power Apps, open your model-driven app in the app designer. Choose Add page, then Generative page, then Describe a page. Type what you want, add up to six Dataverse tables, and select Generate page. You watch the agent outline its plan, write the code and render the result. Then you save and publish.

Way 2

With an AI coding tool. Microsoft now recommends building generative pages with AI code generation tools such as GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude Code. A planner agent proposes the pages, tables and solution first. You approve the plan, and it builds and deploys. This route can create several pages and their supporting tables in one run.

Either way, a person still checks the result. Microsoft is clear that the maker is responsible for validating the code before users rely on it.

Where do generative pages show up?

A generative page can live in three places:

  • In the app navigation, as its own page.
  • Inside a form, in a section or tab. Once the page is set up to accept a record ID, the form passes in the current record automatically. So you can keep the standard form for data entry and add a richer view beside it.
  • Opened from another page or from script, with the record or other inputs passed in.

To see three of these built, with the limits stated plainly, read three screens we built on demo data.

What are 12 ways to use generative pages?

Here are twelve uses for small and mid-sized teams on Dynamics 365. Some come from Microsoft's own examples, three are the screens in our demo, and the rest are common requests.

  1. 1SalesTop accounts board.A ranked gallery of key accounts with revenue and last activity. Microsoft's own examples include an account card gallery and a top accounts dashboard.
  2. 2SalesPipeline board.Opportunities as cards by stage, so reps see the whole pipeline on one screen.
  3. 3SalesAccount 360 on the account form.Relationship health with its reason, win rate, open pipeline by month, contacts and open cases, on one tab before a call.
  4. 4SalesOpportunity command center.The first tab on a deal: revenue, probability, stage, products, overdue follow-ups in red, and the quote.
  5. 5SalesQuote approvals.A list of pending quotes. Tick the ones you are happy with and approve them together. Microsoft shows the same pattern with an order review page that calls a custom API, which is still in preview.
  6. 6ServiceActive cases command center.Case list, status and trend charts, filters and SLA flags on one page.
  7. 7ServiceCustomer history on the case.Past cases and recent activity for the same customer, shown inside the case form.
  8. 8ServiceDocuments beside the case.Files from a SharePoint list shown next to the record. Connector support is still in preview.
  9. 9Operations and fieldJobs on a map.Open work orders or incidents on a map for dispatchers. Microsoft lists "incident reports on a map" as an example prompt.
  10. 10Operations and fieldEquipment gallery with photos.Customer assets or products as picture cards, so people find the right one by sight, not by ID.
  11. 11Leadership and financeRole-based home pages.One start page per role, showing that person's open work.
  12. 12Leadership and financeUnbilled time review.Time entries waiting for approval or billing, by project.

When should you not use a generative page?

Generative pages are not the answer to everything. Pick something else when:

  • The job is simple data entry. A standard form is more consistent and easier to support.
  • You need heavy reporting over a lot of data. Use Power BI. A community tester has noted that generated pages can load data into the browser, which does not suit large volumes.
  • People need to ask questions, not open a screen. Copilot in Dynamics 365 answers questions about your data in a side pane.
  • The need is a conversation or an automated process. Build an agent or workflow in Copilot Studio.
  • You need one control reused across many forms. A PCF code component fits better.
  • Several makers must edit the same page at once. Generative pages do not support co-authoring.

Also expect to iterate. A new prompt can change parts of the page you were happy with, so test after each change.

What do you need to get started?

You need a Dynamics 365 or Power Apps environment with a model-driven app. Microsoft says the maker experience does not need any extra AI or message credits.

For in-browser building, the environment must be in the United States, Great Britain, Australia or Singapore, and prompts are in US English. The AI coding tool route works worldwide on public clouds.

What is the status and licensing (November 2026)?

As of November 2026, generative pages in model-driven apps are generally available. Using Power Platform connectors, Dataverse custom APIs and Application Insights telemetry with generative pages is still in preview. Microsoft does not list a separate end-user license for generative pages. Check your own licensing and admin settings with your partner before you build. Features change often, so confirm details on Microsoft Learn.

Frequently asked questions

What are generative pages in Dynamics 365?

They are pages in model-driven apps that Microsoft's app agent builds from a plain-language description. The agent writes React code that reads and updates your Dataverse data.

Are generative pages generally available?

Yes. Generative pages in model-driven apps are generally available. Using Power Platform connectors and Dataverse custom APIs with them is still in preview.

Does building generative pages cost extra?

Microsoft says the maker experience doesn't require any additional AI or message credits. Users still need a license for the app the page sits in.

What data can a generative page use?

Up to six Dataverse tables per page. Power Platform connectors and Dataverse custom APIs are available in preview.

Can I edit the code?

Yes. You can keep chatting with the agent or edit the code directly. Each save becomes a new iteration, and you can compare iterations within the same editing session.

Do generative pages replace Power BI or Copilot?

No. Use Power BI for heavy analytics, Copilot for questions about your data, and generative pages for focused working screens.

How Dynamics 365 Activate Makes Leaving Salesforce Easier

Switching to Dynamics 365

By Brian BegleySeptember 16, 2026Updated November 10, 20266 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedSeptember 16, 2026
  • TopicSwitching to Dynamics 365
  • Reading time6 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. The Real Reason Companies Don’t Switch CRMs
  2. Microsoft Is Removing Some of That Friction with Dynamics 365 Activate
  3. A Better CRM, Not Just a New CRM
  4. Why More Businesses Are Evaluating Dynamics 365
  5. Why an Experienced Partner Still Matters
  6. Further Reading from Microsoft
  7. How enCloud9 Can Help
  8. Want help with this?

The short answerDynamics 365 Activate is Microsoft’s AI-assisted tool for moving from Salesforce. It assesses a Salesforce environment’s data, customizations, business processes and dependencies, so you see the scope of a move before you start. Microsoft Learn marks it as a preview feature. It cannot decide what should stay, what should go, or how your new CRM should work.

Most companies don’t wake up one morning and decide to replace their CRM. In fact, many stay with a system long after they’ve started questioning it.

Maybe costs keep climbing. Maybe users are frustrated. Maybe reporting has become difficult to maintain. Maybe you’re already invested in Microsoft 365 and wonder why your CRM feels disconnected from the rest of your technology stack. But then reality sets in. You have years of customer data. Custom fields. Workflows. Integrations. Reports. User training.

The Real Reason Companies Don’t Switch CRMs

When people talk about Salesforce versus Dynamics 365, the conversation often centers on features. In reality, that’s usually not what stops companies from making a move. The biggest obstacle is friction.

Organizations worry about what happens to years of customer history. They wonder how much downtime they’ll face, what migration will cost, and whether they’ll end up with the same problems on a different platform.

enCloud9 has had countless conversations with companies that were interested in Dynamics 365 but hesitant to start the process because the migration itself felt overwhelming. That’s understandable.

A CRM is one of the most important systems in your business. It’s where your sales team works, where your customer information lives, and where many of your critical processes take place. The thought of moving everything somewhere new can feel risky.

Microsoft Is Removing Some of That Friction with Dynamics 365 Activate

Microsoft recently introduced Dynamics 365 Activate, a new AI-powered migration and implementation experience for Salesforce environments. Microsoft Learn marks it as a preview feature (checked 10 November 2026). Microsoft says the tool can analyze a Salesforce environment, identify data, business processes, customizations, and dependencies, and provide recommendations that help organizations understand the scope of a migration before they begin.

Dynamics 365 Activate helps organizations get a clearer picture of what’s actually inside their CRM before they start planning a move. That’s important because many businesses have spent years building and modifying their Salesforce environment. Over time, complexity accumulates.

  • Fields nobody uses anymore.
  • Old workflows that still run in the background.
  • Reports created for employees who left years ago.
  • Customizations layered on top of customizations.

Many organizations don’t fully understand how much has accumulated until they begin evaluating a migration.

Dynamics 365 Activate is designed to help uncover those details earlier in the process, making it easier to understand what you’re working with before making major decisions.

A Better CRM, Not Just a New CRM

What’s interesting about Dynamics 365 Activate isn’t the technology itself. It’s what the technology makes possible. For years, a significant portion of a migration project involved figuring out what existed in the current system. If Activate can reduce some of that effort, organizations can spend less time documenting their old CRM and more time planning their future one.

That’s where the real value is. Because the goal shouldn’t be to recreate Salesforce inside Dynamics 365. The goal should be to improve what wasn’t working in the first place.

A migration is one of the few times a business has permission to step back and ask important questions:

  • Do we still need this process?
  • Is this customization adding value?
  • Can we simplify the way our team works?
  • Is our data organized in a way that supports growth?
  • Are we making life easier for our users?

Those are the questions that determine whether a CRM project succeeds. And those questions can’t be answered by software alone. The companies that get the most value from a CRM migration aren’t the ones that move the fastest. They’re the ones that use the opportunity to simplify, modernize, and align their CRM with how the business operates today.

Why More Businesses Are Evaluating Dynamics 365

We’re seeing more companies take a fresh look at Dynamics 365 because they want a CRM that’s more closely aligned with the technology they already use every day. For organizations running Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Power Platform, and Microsoft Copilot, Dynamics 365 feels like a natural extension of the Microsoft ecosystem. Instead of maintaining separate platforms from different vendors, businesses are looking for ways to simplify operations, improve collaboration, and create a more connected user experience.

That doesn’t automatically make Dynamics 365 the right choice for everyone. But it does make the evaluation worth considering, especially when tools like Dynamics 365 Activate are helping reduce some of the barriers traditionally associated with switching platforms.

Why an Experienced Partner Still Matters

Dynamics 365 Activate can help identify customizations, workflows, data structures, and dependencies, but it can’t tell you what should stay, what should go, or how your future CRM should work. That’s where enCloud9 comes in.

A successful CRM migration isn’t about moving everything from Salesforce to Dynamics 365. It’s about taking the opportunity to simplify processes, clean up data, and build a system that better supports your business. While Dynamics 365 Activate helps you understand your current environment, enCloud9 helps you turn that insight into a CRM strategy that works for your team today and can grow with you tomorrow.

Further Reading from Microsoft

If you’d like to learn more about Dynamics 365 Activate and Microsoft’s approach to CRM implementations, these resources provide additional information:

  • Dynamics 365 Activate overview (preview): Microsoft’s official introduction to Dynamics 365 Activate and its vision for simplifying CRM migrations.
  • Accelerate your move to agentic business applications with Dynamics 365 Activate: Learn how Dynamics 365 Activate helps organizations reduce migration friction and move to Dynamics 365 with greater confidence.
  • Overview of Salesforce migration to Dynamics 365: Learn how Dynamics 365 Activate helps assess your Salesforce environment and plan a smoother move to Dynamics 365.

How enCloud9 Can Help

Technology is only part of a successful CRM migration. The bigger challenge is making sure your next CRM helps your business perform better than the one you’re leaving behind.

enCloud9 has helped organizations implement, optimize, and support Microsoft Dynamics 365 for years. We understand that moving from Salesforce isn’t simply a data migration project. It’s an opportunity to improve the way your business manages customer relationships, sales processes, and service operations.

Our team can help you:

  • Evaluate whether Dynamics 365 is the right fit for your organization
  • Assess your current Salesforce environment
  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes and improve data quality
  • Plan and execute a migration strategy
  • Configure Dynamics 365 to align with your business goals
  • Train users and drive adoption
  • Optimize your CRM for long-term success

As Microsoft continues to expand Dynamics 365 Activate, we’re following its development closely and exploring how it can help reduce migration effort for our clients. At the same time, our focus remains on what matters most: helping organizations build CRM systems that support growth, improve productivity, and deliver long-term value.

Whether you’re evaluating Dynamics 365 for the first time or actively planning a migration from Salesforce, enCloud9 can help you understand your options, reduce risk, and create a strategy that supports your business long after go-live. See Move from Salesforce.

How to Improve Dynamics 365 Data Quality: Garbage In, Garbage Out

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyAugust 27, 2026Updated November 10, 20264 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedAugust 27, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. Why do Dynamics 365 data quality problems happen?
  2. How does simpler data entry improve data quality?
  3. Who should own the data in Dynamics 365?
  4. How does automation improve Dynamics 365 data quality?
  5. How do you manage duplicate records before they damage data quality?
  6. How are user adoption and data quality connected?
  7. Why does data quality matter more in the age of AI?
  8. How do you build long-term Dynamics 365 data quality?
  9. What should you read next about Dynamics 365 data quality?
  10. Frequently asked questions
  11. Ready to improve your Dynamics 365 data quality?

The short answerPoor Dynamics 365 data quality builds up over time, not overnight. Duplicates, skipped fields, outdated processes and data nobody owns all add up. Fix it at the source. Simplify data entry, give the data an owner and automate how it is captured. Check for duplicates as routine, and show users why the data matters.

The phrase garbage in, garbage out has been around for decades. It still explains why CRM projects succeed or fail.

Dynamics 365 Sales can give you useful insight into customers, pipeline and performance. If the data going in is incomplete, stale, duplicated or wrong, the reports, forecasts and AI recommendations are unreliable too.

enCloud9 has worked with Dynamics 365 for years and has seen this firsthand. When reports look wrong or users stop trusting the system, companies often blame the CRM. The real problem is usually data quality.

Better data quality does not mean starting over. It means better processes, habits and governance around what goes into the system.

Why do Dynamics 365 data quality problems happen?

They happen slowly, over years. Data quality rarely fails in one moment. It slips through:

  • Duplicate records
  • Fields that people skip
  • Setups that no longer match how the business works
  • Information that nobody owns

Eventually, people stop trusting the system. Cleanup projects help for a while, but the same problems often return months later. That is because the cause is a gap in process and adoption, not a handful of isolated errors.

How does simpler data entry improve data quality?

Simpler entry makes accurate records more likely. Complexity is one of the biggest causes of poor data quality. More required fields, more screens and more steps push users toward shortcuts.

Review your system with these questions:

  • Are all required fields truly necessary?
  • Are your forms laid out for fast, accurate data entry?
  • Are users asked to enter information they don’t actually use?
  • Are there outdated fields that should be removed?
  • Does the CRM reflect how your team works today?

When entry is simple, records stay accurate and current. Over time, that builds Dynamics 365 data quality.

Who should own the data in Dynamics 365?

Specific people or teams should own it. Without that, nobody does. Sales assumes marketing owns customer data. Marketing assumes sales does. Leadership assumes everyone keeps the CRM current.

Organizations with strong data quality name the people or teams who keep accounts, contacts, opportunities and customer information accurate. When ownership is clear, accountability follows.

How does automation improve Dynamics 365 data quality?

Automation captures information the same way every time, so fewer mistakes get in. Manual processes leave room for error.

Dynamics 365 Sales has several options that help:

  • Business rules
  • Power Automate workflows
  • Duplicate detection
  • Integrations with other systems

enCloud9 has seen automation deliver bigger long-term gains than large cleanup projects. The aim is to stop bad data getting in, not just to clean it up afterward.

How do you manage duplicate records before they damage data quality?

Make duplicate detection and review a routine part of CRM administration, not an occasional cleanup. Duplicate contacts and accounts confuse users, distort reports and make the system harder to trust.

Data is far easier to maintain when you are dealing with dozens of duplicates instead of thousands. Microsoft explains how to set up duplicate detection rules on Microsoft Learn (checked 10 November 2026).

How are user adoption and data quality connected?

Users keep data current when they understand why it matters. Many organizations enforce data rules without ever explaining them.

Show people how their data feeds:

  • Forecasting
  • Territory planning
  • Pipeline visibility
  • Customer service
  • Executive reporting

Improving adoption and improving data quality are often the same project.

Why does data quality matter more in the age of AI?

AI tools like Microsoft Copilot cannot fix poor CRM data. They tend to expose data problems that went unnoticed before.

Inaccurate input produces inaccurate insight. Organizations with strong data are better placed to benefit from AI.

How do you build long-term Dynamics 365 data quality?

Treat it as an ongoing commitment, not a one-time project. The most successful CRM systems are not always the most customized. They are the ones where people trust the data.

That trust comes from five things:

  • Simple processes
  • Clear ownership
  • Smart automation
  • Regular maintenance
  • Strong adoption

When a CRM struggles, improving the data you have usually beats replacing the system. Regular care fits a monthly support plan. enCloud9 support plans start at $500 a month for 4 hours on the Stability plan, the minimum plan for new clients.

Some systems need more than routine care. For those, Rescue and Repair costs $500 to $10,000 and takes 8 to 16 weeks, quoted after a short call.

What should you read next about Dynamics 365 data quality?

These enCloud9 posts go deeper on trust, Copilot and adoption:

  • Why Your Sales Pipeline Isn’t Telling the Truth
  • Before You Start Using Copilot, Fix These 7 CRM Data Problems
  • Why Dynamics 365 Adoption Breaks, and Why More Training Won’t Fix It
  • Is Your Dynamics 365 Healthy, or Just “Working”?

Frequently asked questions

Why does Dynamics 365 data quality get worse over time?

It builds up slowly. Duplicates, skipped fields, setups that no longer match the business and data nobody owns all add up until people stop trusting the system.

Is a one-time data cleanup enough?

Usually not. The same problems often return months later, because the cause is process and adoption. Simpler entry, clear ownership and automation stop bad data getting in.

Does data quality affect Copilot?

Yes. AI tools like Microsoft Copilot cannot fix poor CRM data. Inaccurate input produces inaccurate insight, so clean data comes first.

How to Stop Leads From Falling Through the Cracks in Dynamics 365

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleySeptember 9, 2026Updated November 10, 20264 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedSeptember 9, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. Why do leads go cold in Dynamics 365?
  2. Does every lead have an owner?
  3. Does every lead have a next step?
  4. How do you spot leads that have stalled?
  5. Where does automation help?
  6. The Bottom Line
  7. Further Reading
  8. How enCloud9 Can Help
  9. Want help with this?

The short answerLeads go cold in Dynamics 365 when nobody owns them and nobody knows the next step. Fix it four ways: give every lead an owner from day one, give every lead a next step with sequences, review inactive leads and overdue activities regularly, and use Power Automate flows as a safety net for reminders.

What if some of your best sales opportunities are slipping through the cracks without anyone realizing it?

A prospect submits a form, requests a demo, or responds to a marketing campaign. The lead enters Dynamics 365, but no one follows up. Days turn into weeks, and the prospect moves on to a competitor.

The good news is that this is often a process problem, not a CRM problem.

Why do leads go cold in Dynamics 365?

Leads usually go cold because of the process, not the software. Most organizations don’t have a lead generation problem. They have a Dynamics 365 lead management problem.

When clients say they need more leads, enCloud9 first looks at what happens after a lead enters the CRM. Often there are opportunities that were never contacted, assigned or followed up on.

Does every lead have an owner?

It should. One of the most common issues enCloud9 sees is leads sitting in Dynamics 365 without a clear owner.

A lead comes in from the website, an event, a referral, or a marketing campaign. It’s entered into the system, but nobody is specifically responsible for taking the next step.

That may not seem like a big deal at first, but it’s often where the problem starts.

Every lead should have a designated owner from day one. Whether you’re assigning leads automatically or manually, someone needs to be accountable for contacting the prospect and moving the conversation forward.

When everyone owns a lead, nobody owns a lead.

Does every lead have a next step?

Often not: another common red flag is a lead with no activities.

enCloud9 has seen organizations with hundreds of open leads in Dynamics 365, but many have no calls, emails, or tasks associated with them. That’s often a sign the lead has stalled.

One of the best ways to prevent this is with Sequences. A well-designed sequence automatically delivers the next recommended action to the salesperson, whether that’s a call, email, task, or meeting. Instead of wondering who to contact next or what to do next, reps have a clear path to follow.

When your team always knows the next step, leads are far less likely to sit untouched or fall through the cracks.

How do you spot leads that have stalled?

Review inactive leads, overdue activities and records with no recent engagement on a regular schedule. Not every prospect is ready to buy immediately.

Some opportunities take weeks or months to develop. That’s normal.

What isn’t normal is allowing leads to sit untouched for long periods of time without anyone noticing.

One of the best ways to improve Dynamics 365 lead management is to regularly review inactive leads, overdue activities, and records with no recent engagement.

Dynamics 365 makes it easy to create views, dashboards, and reports that identify records that need attention. enCloud9 recommends that sales managers review these records regularly to make sure opportunities aren’t being forgotten.

Where does automation help?

As a safety net, because even good salespeople get busy.

That’s why automation can help reinforce your Dynamics 365 lead management process.

Simple Power Automate flows or Dynamics 365 workflows can notify users when new leads are created, remind sales reps about overdue activities, or alert managers when records have gone untouched for too long.

Automation won’t fix a broken process on its own, but it can help prevent opportunities from slipping through the cracks due to simple oversight.

The Bottom Line

enCloud9 has worked with Dynamics 365 clients who were ready to spend more money on advertising, SEO, events, and lead generation because they believed they needed more leads.

In reality, they already had opportunities sitting in their CRM.

What they needed was better Dynamics 365 lead management.

When every lead has an owner, every lead has a next step, and managers have visibility into stalled records, the number of missed opportunities drops dramatically.

Before you focus on generating more leads, make sure you’re getting the most out of the ones you already have.

If leads are falling through the cracks in your Dynamics 365 environment, the issue is rarely the software itself. More often, it’s a combination of process gaps, inconsistent follow-up, lack of visibility, or missing automation.

enCloud9 has spent years helping organizations improve Dynamics 365 lead management, streamline sales processes, and build systems that help sales teams stay on top of every opportunity. From lead assignment and dashboards to Power Automate reminders and workflow automation, enCloud9 can help you build a process that keeps leads moving and reduces the risk of missed opportunities.

How To Track the Last Activity Date in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyFebruary 13, 2025Updated November 10, 20262 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedFebruary 13, 2025
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time2 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. Why track last and next activity dates?
  2. How do you create last and next activity date fields in Dynamics 365?
  3. Where should the new fields go?
  4. When do the rollup fields fill in?
  5. About enCloud9
  6. Want help with this?

The short answerMicrosoft Dynamics 365 does not include a built-in last activity date. Add two rollup columns to the lead table: Last Activity Date, the maximum Actual End date of its activities, and Next Activity Due Date, the minimum Due Date of its open activities. Then add both to your forms and views so reps see who needs follow-up.

The steps below show how, and the full tutorial is also on YouTube.

Watch the full tutorial on YouTube: Easily Track Last & Next Activity Dates in Dynamics 365

Why track last and next activity dates?

Knowing the last activity date allows sales teams to quickly see when they last engaged with a lead, contact, or account. If a prospect hasn’t been contacted in a while, it might be time to re-engage.

Meanwhile, the next activity due date ensures that sales reps never miss an upcoming call, meeting, or email. This field provides a clear schedule of future interactions, improving responsiveness and boosting conversion rates.

How do you create last and next activity date fields in Dynamics 365?

To automate activity tracking in Dynamics 365, follow these steps:

Step 1: Create the Last Activity Date Field

  • Go to Power Apps (make.powerapps.com) and open the Lead table.
  • Create a new column called Last Activity Date.
  • Set the data type to Date and Time, format it as Date Only, and change its behavior to a Rollup field.
  • Configure the rollup settings: select Activities as the related entity, and set the aggregation to Maximum (Max) of the Actual End Date of the activity.
  • Save and close the configuration.

Step 2: Create the Next Activity Due Field

  • Repeat the above steps, naming the field Next Activity Due Date.
  • Set the aggregation to Minimum (Min) of the Due Date instead of Max.
  • Filter the Activity Records to use only Open Activities.
  • Save the field and add it to the form.

Where should the new fields go?

Once the fields are created, add them to your Lead forms for easy access. You should also include them in your Open Leads views to monitor past and future activities at a glance.

When do the rollup fields fill in?

Existing records fill in about 12 hours after you create the column. After that, values refresh about every hour, or right away with Recalculate on the form. See rollup columns on Microsoft Learn (checked 10 November 2026).

By adding these rollup fields, your team can stay organized, follow up on time, and never miss a critical opportunity.

Add the two columns, then check a few leads the next day to confirm the dates filled in.

Mastering Lead Management in Dynamics 365: Igniting Your Sales Pipeline

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyNovember 15, 2023Updated November 10, 20263 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedNovember 15, 2023
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time3 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. How do leads get into Dynamics 365?
  2. How do you qualify and score leads?
  3. How do you route leads to the right seller?
  4. How do you nurture leads until they are ready to buy?
  5. What happens when a lead is qualified?
  6. Which lead reports should you watch?
  7. How do sales and marketing share leads in Dynamics 365?
  8. How can enCloud9 help with lead management?
  9. Frequently asked questions
  10. Ready to ignite your sales pipeline?

The short answerDynamics 365 Sales manages a lead from first contact to a qualified opportunity. Leads from your website, social media and email campaigns land in one place. You score them, route them to the right seller, nurture them with automated follow-up, and convert qualified leads into opportunities. Reports then show which sources and nurturing steps work best.

Update, November 2026

What changed since this post was written?

The Microsoft features in this post were checked 10 November 2026 on Microsoft Learn. Dynamics 365 Sales now offers predictive lead scoring, assignment rules and an AI agent that researches and engages leads. Microsoft also recommends Power Automate flows instead of classic workflows for new automation.

The original post follows, with those features linked where it mentions them.

How do leads get into Dynamics 365?

Dynamics 365 collects leads from your website, social media, email campaigns and other sources in one central place.

Lead entry forms can be tailored to your business, so you gather the details your team needs from the start.

How do you qualify and score leads?

Start by setting the criteria that make a lead ready for sales, such as demographics, lead source and engagement level.

Lead scoring then gives each lead a number based on its attributes and interactions. A higher score means a better chance of converting, so sellers know where to start.

Microsoft’s predictive lead scoring builds that score from your own history. It needs at least 40 qualified and 40 disqualified leads to train a model (checked 10 November 2026). Predictive scoring is part of Sales Insights; a Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise license includes 1,500 scored records a month (Microsoft Learn, checked 10 November 2026).

How do you route leads to the right seller?

Assignment rules route each lead by geographic territory, product expertise and workload, so it reaches the right person fast.

Faster response times mean more chances to convert. In Dynamics 365 Sales, assignment rules assign new leads to sellers or teams automatically once a rule is active (checked 10 November 2026).

How do you nurture leads until they are ready to buy?

Automated follow-up sends personalized emails, newsletters and targeted promotions.

Dynamics 365 keeps each lead’s interaction and engagement history, so your team can tailor what it sends next. That might mean sharing more information, answering a concern or offering an exclusive deal.

For new automation, Microsoft recommends Power Automate flows rather than classic workflows (checked 10 November 2026).

What happens when a lead is qualified?

A qualified lead moves into the opportunity stage, where sellers build tailored solutions and proposals.

When you qualify a lead, Dynamics 365 can create the account, contact and opportunity for you. What it creates depends on how your admin set it up (checked 10 November 2026).

Which lead reports should you watch?

Track conversion rates, lead sources and how well each nurturing approach works.

Those numbers show where to put your budget and your people. The aim is more leads becoming opportunities, and a better return on what you spend to get them.

How do sales and marketing share leads in Dynamics 365?

Sales and marketing work in the same system, so leads move from marketing to sales without being re-entered.

Marketing automation brings leads in. Sellers then use the same lead data to close deals. More leads that convert mean more revenue and profit.

How can enCloud9 help with lead management?

enCloud9 has been a Microsoft Partner since 2008. It helps small and medium-sized businesses set up lead scoring, assignment and follow-up in Dynamics 365 Sales. The Sales Accelerator sets up Dynamics 365 Sales for your pipeline for $7,500.

Frequently asked questions

How does lead scoring work in Dynamics 365?

Predictive lead scoring uses a machine learning model trained on your past leads to score open ones. It needs at least 40 qualified and 40 disqualified leads from the training period.

Can Dynamics 365 assign leads automatically?

Yes. Assignment rules in Dynamics 365 Sales assign new leads to sellers or teams based on conditions you set, such as territory or product.

What happens when you qualify a lead?

The lead closes as qualified. Dynamics 365 can then create an account, contact and opportunity from it, depending on how your admin set it up.
