Dataverse Storage Warning: What It Means and What to Do

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyNovember 3, 2026Updated November 10, 20264 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedNovember 3, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. What does a Dataverse storage warning mean?
  2. What is using up your Dataverse storage?
  3. Can you ignore a Dataverse storage warning?
  4. What happens when you go over your Dataverse storage limit?
  5. How can enCloud9 help with Dataverse storage?
  6. Frequently asked questions
  7. Don't ignore the warning

The short answerA Dataverse storage warning means your tenant has less than 15% of its database, file or log storage left. Microsoft emails admins every week, warns again under 5%, and again once you go over. Over the limit, you can’t create, copy, restore or recover environments. Production keeps running, and Microsoft is rolling out stricter limits for sandboxes.

What does a Dataverse storage warning mean?

Most companies don’t think about Dataverse storage until Microsoft warns them. By then, the issue may have been growing for months without anyone realizing it.

Microsoft Dataverse sits at the heart of Dynamics 365 and Power Platform environments. It has three kinds of storage: database, file and log. Microsoft sends the first warning when any of the three has less than 15% left, the next under 5%, and the last when you go over. Admins and makers get the emails every week, and a banner shows in the Power Platform admin center and your Dynamics 365 apps.

What is using up your Dataverse storage?

Every customer record, attachment, workflow, integration, audit log, and business process adds to your Dataverse storage usage. The problem is that storage growth isn’t always obvious. It happens little by little until one day Microsoft starts sending notifications.

At that point, most businesses don’t know:

  • What’s actually consuming storage
  • Which environments are growing the fastest
  • Whether growth is normal or excessive
  • If additional storage is really needed
  • How much they’re spending on storage they may not actually need

Without those answers, you’re left guessing. The good news is you don’t have to guess. enCloud9’s free Microsoft Dataverse Storage Analysis helps you understand what’s driving storage growth, identify potential risks, and create a plan before capacity issues impact your business.

Can you ignore a Dataverse storage warning?

When Dataverse storage warning notifications start showing up, it’s easy to push them to the bottom of the priority list. After all, everything is still working. But that’s exactly why these notifications catch people off guard.

Storage issues rarely become urgent overnight. They build quietly in the background until your team suddenly needs to create an environment, perform a restore, refresh a sandbox, or support a deployment. That’s when storage becomes everyone’s problem. The sooner you understand what’s driving your storage growth, the more options you’ll have to address it.

What happens when you go over your Dataverse storage limit?

Ignoring a Microsoft Dataverse storage notification doesn’t stop storage from growing. Once you go over, Microsoft’s capacity rules work in stages. Microsoft is rolling out the stricter checks, so the 30 and 90 day stages apply once they reach your tenant:

  • The day you go over: you can’t create, copy, restore or recover environments.
  • After 30 days: your sandbox environments lock to administrators only.
  • After 90 days: nobody can sign in to those sandboxes, admins included.

Production environments never enter the admin-only or blocked stages, so your production apps keep running. Microsoft’s capacity rules checked on Microsoft Learn, 10 November 2026. But anything that needs a restore, a copy or a test environment is blocked. The longer you wait, the greater the risk of unexpected costs, unnecessary storage purchases, and operational headaches.

A simple assessment today from enCloud9 can help prevent a much more expensive problem tomorrow. A proactive assessment is almost always easier, less expensive, and far less disruptive than reacting after the fact.

How can enCloud9 help with Dataverse storage?

enCloud9’s free Dataverse Storage Analysis shows what is using your storage, where it is growing and what to do next.

enCloud9’s Microsoft Dataverse Storage Analysis gives you a clear picture of what’s happening inside your environment. We’ll identify what’s consuming your storage, where growth is occurring, and what steps you can take to reduce risk before it impacts your business.

We’ll also help you determine whether additional Dataverse storage is actually necessary, or whether you can reclaim capacity through better governance, data cleanup, and optimization. Extra database storage lists at $40 per GB per month ($480 a year), and $48 on pay-as-you-go, so cleaning up often pays for itself.

And because storage management isn’t a one-time project, many customers pair that analysis with one of our ongoing support plans. enCloud9’s managed services team helps monitor your environment, provide governance guidance, and stay ahead of problems before they turn into costly disruptions.

The companies that avoid storage headaches aren’t necessarily the ones with the biggest budgets. They’re the ones that take action before small issues become big ones.

Frequently asked questions

Will Dynamics 365 CRM stop working?

No. Your production apps keep running. But anything that needs a restore, a copy or a test environment is blocked.

Can we turn off Microsoft’s storage warning emails or notifications?

No. Admins get the emails every week with no opt-out. The banner can be dismissed for seven days, then it comes back.

What takes up the most Dataverse storage?

Old emails and their attachments, notes and attachments, audit history, logs, and environments nobody uses anymore. The analysis shows the tables using the most space and the ones growing fastest.

What is the free Dataverse Storage Analysis?

A one-hour Teams meeting with an enCloud9 consultant. We find what is using your storage and how fast it is growing, and work with you on a plan to get back under your limit. It is free, and open to any organization.

Microsoft Introduces 30 New Dynamics 365 CRM Skills for Copilot

Copilot and AI

By Brian BegleyOctober 14, 2026Updated November 10, 20263 min read

At a glance

  • TopicCopilot and AI
  • Reading time3 minutes

  5. How enCloud9 Can Help
  6. Want help with this?

The short answerMicrosoft added 30 pre-built CRM skills that bring Dynamics 365 data into Copilot, built on more than 180 Dynamics 365 tools across Sales, Customer Service and Customer Insights. Sellers get help with deal risks, meeting prep and CRM updates. Service reps get case history, case proposals and draft replies, without custom workflows.

Figures from Microsoft's October 8, 2026 announcement, linked below.

In an October 8, 2026 announcement, Microsoft introduced 30 new Dynamics 365 CRM Skills designed to bring customer intelligence directly into Copilot and the flow of work, helping sales and service teams spend less time searching for information and more time serving customers. For businesses already invested in Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365, this update offers an important look at how AI is transforming CRM from a system of record into a system of action.

The Shift from CRM as a System of Record to a System of Action

Traditionally, CRM systems have functioned as systems of record. They store customer information, sales activities, service history, and marketing engagement data. While that information is valuable, employees have often needed to leave their workflow to access it or update it.

Microsoft’s latest announcement signals a shift toward a more active role for CRM. Rather than simply storing information, Dynamics 365 can now help employees make decisions, complete tasks, and move customer interactions forward through Copilot-powered experiences.

This approach helps reduce context switching, one of the biggest productivity challenges facing modern organizations. Instead of jumping between email, Teams, CRM records, and other business applications, employees can access customer intelligence directly within the tools they use every day.

What Are the 30 New CRM Skills?

The most significant part of Microsoft’s announcement is the introduction of 30 pre-built CRM skills that connect Dynamics 365 expertise with Copilot experiences. Microsoft states these skills are built on more than 180 Dynamics 365 tools across Sales, Customer Service, and Customer Insights, providing ready-to-use capabilities without requiring organizations to build custom workflows from scratch.

For sales teams, these skills can help:

  • Analyze opportunities and identify potential risks
  • Build competitive sales strategies
  • Prepare for customer meetings and leadership reviews
  • Access customer and account context more efficiently
  • Convert meeting outcomes into suggested CRM updates and next actions

These capabilities allow sellers to spend less time on administrative work and more time focused on customer relationships and revenue-generating activities.

For customer service teams, the new skills can help:

  • Review customer and case history
  • Transform correspondence into structured case proposals
  • Research relevant answers and solutions
  • Draft customer communications
  • Surface important account information within existing workflows

Rather than searching multiple systems for customer context, service representatives can use AI-powered assistance informed by Dynamics 365 data to support faster and more informed customer interactions.

Microsoft also notes that marketers can use these skills to create consent-aware outreach and develop brand-compliant content while remaining connected to customer information and business processes.

Why This Matters for Businesses

With Copilot and CRM skills working together, customer context, recommendations and actions can appear at the moment employees need them, inside the tools they already use, instead of employees gathering information from several systems and entering updates by hand.

Further Reading

For additional information from Microsoft, check out:

  • Bringing CRM into the flow of work and agents into business process for sales and service teams
  • Microsoft Copilot

How enCloud9 Can Help

As Microsoft continues to expand Copilot, Dynamics 365, and AI-powered business applications, understanding how these tools fit into your organization becomes increasingly important.

Whether you’re exploring Microsoft Copilot, evaluating Dynamics 365, or looking for practical ways to integrate AI into your sales and service operations, our team can help you identify opportunities, build a strategy, and maximize the value of your Microsoft investment.

We help organizations move beyond the hype and focus on real business outcomes through thoughtful planning, adoption, and optimization.

The short answerMicrosoft deprecated sales usage reports in Dynamics 365 Sales on December 1, 2025. As an alternative, it offers a sample Power BI report for sales usage reporting, which you customize and maintain yourself, without Microsoft support. Before then, an admin turned the reports on in App Settings, and managers read them under Sales Analytics.

Update, November 2026

What changed since 2024?

Microsoft deprecated sales usage reports effective December 1, 2025. As an alternative, Microsoft offers a sample Power BI report for sales usage reporting. Microsoft says you customize and maintain it yourself, and it does not support the sample. Details are on Microsoft Learn.

Microsoft’s own page describes four usage reports, for opportunities, leads, accounts and contacts.

The original 2024 post follows, as Brian wrote it.

Dynamics 365 Sales is a powerful platform offering extensive tools to enhance sales processes. Among these tools, Sales Usage Reports are particularly valuable for providing insights into sales performance and operational efficiency. Enabling these reports can help sales managers and teams understand their performance, identify areas for improvement, and make data-driven decisions.

Why enable sales usage reports?

Five benefits for sales managers and their teams.

  1. 1DecisionsData-driven decision making.With access to detailed sales usage reports, sales managers can make informed decisions based on concrete data rather than intuition. This leads to more effective strategies and better resource allocation.
  2. 2PlanningEnhanced sales forecasting.Accurate forecasting is essential for planning and resource management. Sales usage reports provide historical data that can improve the accuracy of sales forecasts.
  3. 3ProcessImproved sales efficiency.By analyzing activity logs and conversion rates, sales teams can identify inefficient practices and streamline their processes. This leads to higher productivity and better use of time and resources.
  4. 4CustomersBetter customer relationships.Understanding customer behavior and satisfaction helps in building stronger relationships. Sales usage reports provide insights that can be used to personalize interactions and improve customer service.
  5. 5TeamPerformance tracking and motivation.Regularly reviewing individual and team performance metrics helps in setting clear goals and expectations. Recognizing top performers and addressing areas for improvement can motivate the sales team to achieve better results.

How do you enable sales usage reports?

Three steps, done once by someone with admin rights.

  1. Log in to Dynamics 365 Sales.Start by logging into your Dynamics 365 Sales account. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to access the settings required for enabling sales usage reports.
  2. Navigate to Settings.Once logged in, navigate to the bottom left corner of the interface. Select "App Settings" from the "Sales" menu. This section contains various configuration options for your sales app.
  3. Enable Sales Usage Reports.Within App Settings, locate the toggle switch for "Sales usage reports." Turn on this toggle to enable the feature. After enabling, select "Save" to apply the changes.

What do sales usage reports show?

Sales Usage Reports in Dynamics 365 provide a comprehensive view of sales activities and outcomes, operational metrics, and key performance indicators (KPIs), allowing sales managers to analyze opportunities and leads to enhance team performance. The reports offer valuable information for both sales managers and salespeople.

To access Sales Usage Reports, navigate to Sales Analytics on the left side navigation. These reports include several key metrics and insights:

1. Sales performance metrics

  • Revenue analysis: track revenue generated over specific periods, allowing for trend analysis and performance tracking.
  • Sales pipeline: monitor the flow of deals through different stages, from initial contact to closing.
  • Conversion rates: analyze conversion rates at each stage of the sales process to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement.

2. Activity tracking

  • Call and email logs: review logs of sales calls and emails to understand engagement levels with prospects and customers.
  • Meeting insights: track the frequency and outcomes of meetings, providing a clear picture of sales team activities.

3. Customer insights

  • Customer segmentation: segment customers by criteria such as industry, size and buying behavior to tailor sales strategies.
  • Customer satisfaction: measure satisfaction through feedback and surveys, enabling proactive improvements.

4. Sales team performance

  • Individual performance: evaluate individual sales representatives, identifying top performers and those needing additional support or training.
  • Team collaboration: assess how well the team collaborates and shares information, which is crucial for closing complex deals.

Learn more about how to view operational metrics and KPIs in usage reports on Microsoft Learn.

As you can see from the illustration below, the report gives you valuable information about contacts, leads, opportunities and accounts. Sales managers, you can easily see from the Sales Usage Report which user has created or updated the most contacts, leads, opportunities or accounts.

Conclusion

Enabling Sales Usage Reports in Dynamics 365 Sales is a straightforward process that offers significant benefits. By following the steps outlined above, sales managers can unlock valuable insights that drive performance improvements and strategic decision-making. The detailed metrics and analyses provided by these reports empower sales teams to operate more efficiently, understand their customers better, and ultimately achieve greater success.

For more detailed instructions on enabling sales usage reports for your organization, visit Microsoft Learn.

Frequently asked questions

Are sales usage reports still available in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Microsoft deprecated sales usage reports effective December 1, 2025. As an alternative, Microsoft offers a sample Power BI report for sales usage reporting, which you customize and maintain yourself.

Where do you turn on sales usage reports?

In the Sales app, go to App Settings in the lower left corner of the page, then turn on the Sales usage reports toggle and select Save.

Where do you view sales usage reports?

Select Sales Analytics in the left side navigation of the Sales app.

What do sales usage reports show?

Sales performance, activity tracking, customer insights and sales team performance, including which user has created or updated the most contacts, leads, opportunities or accounts.

What was wrong with BG Peterson’s systems?

BG Peterson is a long-standing mechanical services company based in Omaha, Nebraska, providing HVAC, plumbing and facility solutions. As the business grew, it needed better visibility into customer interactions and more reliable financial processes.

BG Peterson had Dynamics 365 Sales for CRM and Business Central for financial management, but struggled to get consistent value from either. On the financial side, ongoing issues in Business Central created bottlenecks and confusion. They centered on bank reconciliations and account balances, sales tax calculations and refunds, month-end and year-end close, and reporting inconsistencies.

Instead of improving efficiency, these challenges created extra manual work and made it difficult for the team to trust their data.

What did enCloud9 change?

enCloud9 first implemented a basic Dynamics 365 Sales environment. It centralizes contacts and accounts, tracks activities and communication history, and gives the team a simple, usable CRM foundation. The work included data import and cleanup, so existing customer and contact data was structured correctly and ready for use in Dynamics 365.

The engagement then shifted into ongoing support and optimization, primarily within Business Central. Working closely with the BG Peterson team, enCloud9 resolved bank reconciliation issues and cleaned up and reorganized general ledger accounts. It supported month-end and year-end close and addressed sales tax calculation and reporting challenges. It also created and tested new company environments to isolate issues.

The team also made targeted Business Central customizations, such as salesperson-related adjustments, and helped troubleshoot and stabilize financial reports in Power BI.

What changed day to day?

The engagement was more of a stabilization and support effort than a traditional transformation project. Still, the improvements made a meaningful difference in day-to-day operations. Financial processes and reporting are more reliable, and the team has more confidence in its Business Central data. Less time goes to troubleshooting recurring system issues, and the team has ongoing access to expert support.

Implementing the software was only the first step. Pairing the CRM setup with hands-on Business Central support moved BG Peterson from frustration and uncertainty to a more stable system.

What changed for PriceMDs?

PriceMDs offers healthcare solutions that help organizations reduce costs while improving access to medications and patient services. Its operations rely on accurate data, efficient workflows and visibility across multiple processes. Before working with enCloud9, PriceMDs was using monday CRM.

It needed a system to manage patient and prescription data across multiple processes, support custom business logic that out-of-the-box CRM does not handle, improve visibility into operations and reporting, and keep data consistent and reliable.

As the business grew, new needs appeared: more workflows and integrations, more data volume, and more functionality without losing stability.

What did enCloud9 build?

enCloud9 implemented Dynamics 365 and configured it around how PriceMDs actually works, with custom entities, workflows, plugins and data structures.

Once PriceMDs saw what Dynamics 365 could do, the scope expanded. enCloud9 supported the development of a medication Pricing Portal, enabled integration with external systems like Tive and Ship 24, and improved data management, reporting and automation.

The project delivered a pharmacist portal and electronic signatures through Document Core Pack and Adobe Sign.

What changed day to day?

Home/Blog/Is Your Dynamics 365 Healthy, or Just “Working”?

Is Your Dynamics 365 Healthy, or Just “Working”?

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyMarch 11, 2026Updated November 10, 20265 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedMarch 11, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time5 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. What are leaders really asking about Dynamics 365?
  2. What does enCloud9 see in real Dynamics 365 systems?
  3. What is the difference between healthy and technically working?
  4. What does a healthy Dynamics 365 system look like in real life?
  5. Is your Dynamics 365 healthy, or just working?
  6. Frequently asked questions
  7. Start with a health check

The short answerA healthy Dynamics 365 system does four things. People rely on it without being forced. Leaders trust its reports without double-checking. Forms and timelines feel simple, not heavy. Security and automation are governed well enough to change safely. A system can be live and stable and still fail these tests, because most systems drift rather than fail.

Ask your leaders whether Dynamics 365 is actually working. You’ll often hear “It’s live,” “It’s stable” or “People log in.” Those answers only show that the system exists.

A healthy system earns trust, drives real behavior and supports the business instead of slowing it down. Health is an ongoing standard, not a one-time cleanup.

enCloud9 helps teams get real value from Dynamics 365: support for revenue, better forecasting and easier daily work. Most environments don’t fail outright. They drift. Reports stop matching, adoption slips and spreadsheets come back.

That is why ongoing attention matters, and why many enCloud9 clients use monthly Dynamics 365 support. Support plans start at $500 a month.

What are leaders really asking about Dynamics 365?

Leaders rarely care whether the system is up. They want to know four things:

  • Can we trust the data?
  • Does the team run the business in Dynamics 365, or work around it?
  • Is it simple enough that people don’t avoid it?
  • Will it hold up as the business changes?

Microsoft’s own implementation guidance makes the same point: change management doesn’t end at go-live (checked 10 November 2026 on Microsoft Learn). enCloud9 stays involved after launch so the CRM keeps delivering value. Learn more about enCloud9’s implementation and post-implementation services.

What does enCloud9 see in real Dynamics 365 systems?

enCloud9 sees where that guidance meets reality. Companies implement, train users and go live. Later, friction shows up:

  • Forecasts don’t line up.
  • Adoption is uneven.
  • People doubt the reports.
  • Changes feel risky.

Someone usually says the company should be getting more from the system. They’re right. A healthy system does four things:

  • People rely on it without being forced.
  • Leaders trust it without double-checking.
  • It feels simple, not heavy.
  • It is governed well enough to change safely.

When one of these breaks, the system may still work technically. It stops working as a business tool.

enCloud9 sees the biggest gains when system health and pipeline health are fixed together, especially at a seasonal reset like spring. See enCloud9’s strategies for a healthier sales pipeline in Dynamics 365.

What is the difference between healthy and technically working?

A technically working system stores data. A healthy system runs the business.

Closing that gap rarely means starting over. It takes making the system easier to use, easier to trust and easier to manage.

enCloud9 recommends a Dynamics 365 System Health Check. Nothing has to be broken. The check finds what helps, what hurts and where small changes add value.

For systems that fall short, enCloud9’s Rescue and Repair fixes what is slowing the CRM down. It costs $500 to $10,000 and takes 8 to 16 weeks, quoted after a short call.

What does a healthy Dynamics 365 system look like in real life?

It shows four traits. Each one is easy to spot once you know what to look for.

1. People actually use it

People use the system because it helps them do their jobs, not because they’re told to. Reps log data as they work, not right before forecast calls. Service teams work from timelines, not email inboxes.

One enCloud9 client put it simply: “It’s faster to just do it in Dynamics 365 now.” That’s the goal. Constant work done around the system points to a system design problem, not a user behavior problem.

2. Reports are trusted

Watch your meetings. In an unhealthy system, meetings turn into debates about whose numbers are right. In a healthy one, meetings focus on decisions.

Refreshing your data helps. Start with enCloud9’s guide to cleaning your CRM data in Dynamics 365, and two short videos:

  • How to clean up CRM data with bulk delete in Dynamics 365 (enCloud9 on YouTube)
  • How to set up duplicate detection rules in Dynamics 365 (enCloud9 on YouTube)

Microsoft documents both tools on Microsoft Learn: bulk deletion jobs and duplicate detection rules (checked 10 November 2026).

enCloud9’s approach is to tighten definitions, clean up the places data comes in, and align reports with how the business measures success.

3. Forms and timelines feel simple

Healthy systems don’t feel heavy. Cluttered forms and noisy timelines drive users away.

enCloud9 often finds records with dozens of unused fields, tabs nobody opens, and required fields nobody understands. The healthiest systems are plain on purpose. They show only what people need, laid out clearly. Adoption improves quickly when they are.

4. Security and automation are intentional

In an unhealthy system, people are afraid to change anything. Nobody knows what the automation does, and access is broader than it should be.

Healthy systems have clear ownership, thoughtful automation, and security based on real roles, not old setups. To start cleaning up, read Dynamics 365 Optimization Simplified.

Is your Dynamics 365 healthy, or just working?

If you aren’t confident you’re getting full value from Dynamics 365, your setup probably isn’t aligned with how you work.

A healthy environment should make work easier, build trust and reduce friction. A System Health Check gives you an honest assessment and finds the small changes with the biggest impact.

Frequently asked questions

What is a Dynamics 365 System Health Check?

An honest review of your Dynamics 365 system. It finds what helps, what hurts and the small changes with the biggest impact. Nothing has to be broken to book one.

Do we need to rebuild Dynamics 365 to fix it?

Rarely. The gap between working and healthy usually closes by making the system easier to use, easier to trust and easier to manage.

How do we know our system has drifted?

Forecasts don’t line up, adoption is uneven, people doubt the reports, spreadsheets come back and changes feel risky.

The short answerIn November 2026, Customer Insights added reusable segment templates and business unit access control. From November 15, Power Platform stops creating new unmanaged developer environments and Dataverse for Teams environments. After November 30, record-level copresence and Power Automate’s Describe it to design it are no longer available. Release Planner retires by November 15.

This is enCloud9’s monthly roundup of what changed in Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform it runs on. Every item links to the Microsoft page it came from, checked 10 November 2026.

Microsoft no longer publishes twice-yearly release plans, so changes now arrive month by month. Read how Microsoft updates Dynamics 365 now for the background.

What is new in Customer Insights - Journeys?

The November 2026 update of Customer Insights - Journeys (release 1.3.2529.71) brings three changes (checked 10 November 2026):

  • Reusable segment templates, generally available. Pick a built-in template, such as event attendance or email engagement, or save your own segment query as a template.
  • A customizable consent list in double opt-in emails. You choose how purposes and topics appear when people confirm their choices.
  • Named, color-coded segment groups. Complex segments are easier to review at a glance.

What is new in Customer Insights - Data?

Two features became generally available in November 2026 (checked 10 November 2026):

  • Admins can show or hide columns and tables in the segment and measure builders, so users see only the data they need.
  • Admins can control access to customer profiles, segments and measures by business unit.

Microsoft also removed four preview features from Customer Insights - Data on November 2, 2026: Dialog with data, Create segments with Copilot, the Copilot help pane and the Copilot consent settings (checked 10 November 2026).

What changes in Power Platform on November 15?

Two kinds of environment can no longer be created from November 15, 2026 (checked 10 November 2026).

Unmanaged developer environments. Microsoft deprecated them. Existing ones are suspended starting December 15, 2026 and deleted starting January 15, 2027. Developer environments that are managed environments aren’t affected. Each user can now create one managed developer environment.

Dataverse for Teams environments. These are deprecated too. Existing ones keep working until September 15, 2027, when any not upgraded to Dataverse are suspended. They are decommissioned on October 30, 2027.

To find them, open the Power Platform admin center and go to Manage, then Environments. For unmanaged developer environments, filter where Type is Developer and Managed is No. For Dataverse for Teams environments, filter where Type is Microsoft Teams.

What retires on November 30?

  • Record-level copresence in model-driven apps. Users will no longer see who else is working on the same record. Record sharing isn’t affected.
  • Describe it to design it in Power Automate. Makers can no longer create cloud flows by describing them. Existing flows aren’t deleted or moved.
  • Copresence in Power Apps plans. Plans no longer show other authors, so only one person should edit a plan at a time.
  • Create descriptions using AI for model-driven apps. Makers write app descriptions by hand. Existing descriptions aren’t affected.

All four dates were checked 10 November 2026 on Microsoft Learn.

What changed in Project Operations?

The November 2026 release of Project Operations Core (version 4.173.1.38) adds the following (checked 10 November 2026):

  • A Policy Authoring Assistant, an agent that reviews the policy documents behind the Activity Approvals Agent
  • A full-screen mode for the task grid
  • Weekly Time Entry Notes, in preview
  • New version numbering from version 4.173, which Microsoft says changes numbering only

Where does Microsoft announce Dynamics 365 changes now?

On the AI at Work roadmap, formerly the Microsoft 365 Roadmap.

Microsoft told partners in September 2026 that it is moving from twice-yearly release waves to continuous roadmap communications. It is archiving its release plans on Microsoft Learn and retiring Release Planner by November 15, 2026 (checked 10 November 2026).

Microsoft says the change affects roadmap communications only. Release schedules, deployment, Message Center notices and documentation stay the same.

What should you do this month?

  • Find any unmanaged developer environments. Before December 15, convert them to managed environments (users need premium licenses) or move their solutions to a sandbox.
  • Tell makers that Describe it to design it retires on November 30.
  • Bookmark the AI at Work roadmap, and update any links to Release Planner.
  • If you use Customer Insights, try segment templates on your next campaign.

Frequently asked questions

Can we still create a developer environment after November 15, 2026?

Only a managed developer environment, one per user. New unmanaged developer environments can’t be created from November 15, 2026.

What happens to existing unmanaged developer environments?

Microsoft suspends them starting December 15, 2026 and deletes them starting January 15, 2027. Before then, convert them to managed environments if your users have premium licenses, or export the solutions and move them to a sandbox.

Where do we find upcoming Dynamics 365 features now?

On Microsoft’s AI at Work roadmap. Microsoft is retiring Release Planner by November 15, 2026 and archiving its release plans on Microsoft Learn.

Which Dynamics 365 Customizations Are Worth It (And Which Ones We Usually Advise Against)

Admin and how-to

By Brian BegleyOctober 7, 2026Updated November 10, 20264 min read

At a glance

  • PublishedOctober 7, 2026
  • TopicAdmin and how-to
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. Which Dynamics 365 customizations are worth it?
  2. Which customizations should you avoid?
  3. How do you decide before building one?
  4. The Bottom Line on Dynamics 365 Customizations
  5. Further Reading
  6. Need Help Deciding Which Dynamics 365 Customizations Are Worth Keeping?
  7. Want help with this?

The short answerThe Dynamics 365 customizations usually worth it are role-based forms, workflow and process automation, integrations that end duplicate data entry, dashboards that support decisions, and custom fields with a clear purpose. Avoid fields added just in case, rebuilding your old CRM, customizing around a broken process, complex code without a business case, and approvals for everything.

Have you ever opened a Dynamics 365 account record and wondered, “Do we really need all of this?”

A field gets added. Then another. Someone requests a custom form. A workflow gets built to handle a unique situation. A few years later, users are scrolling through pages of information they rarely use, and simple updates feel anything but simple. The problem isn’t Dynamics 365 customizations themselves. Some Dynamics 365 customizations can improve adoption, reporting, and productivity. The challenge is knowing which customizations add real business value and which ones simply add more complexity. After years of implementing, optimizing and supporting Dynamics 365, enCloud9 has seen both.

Which Dynamics 365 customizations are worth it?

Five usually are: role-based forms, process automation, integrations that end duplicate entry, dashboards that support decisions, and custom fields with a clear purpose. In fact, some can make the system significantly more useful and easier for employees to adopt.

Role-Based Forms

Different teams need different information. Sales reps don’t need to see everything that managers need, and managers don’t need to see everything that service teams use. One of the most valuable Dynamics 365 customizations is tailoring forms to specific user groups. Cleaner screens make it easier for users to find what they need and enter accurate data.

Workflow and Process Automation

When employees perform the same task over and over, automation can be a huge win. Automated lead assignment, follow-up reminders, task creation, and notifications are Dynamics 365 customizations that often deliver immediate value. The best automations eliminate repetitive work without making the process harder to follow.

Integrations That Eliminate Duplicate Data Entry

Few things frustrate users more than entering the same data into multiple systems. Dynamics 365 customizations that connect CRM data with Outlook, ERP systems, marketing platforms, or customer service applications can save time while improving data quality.

Dashboards That Support Better Decisions

A well-designed dashboard helps leaders quickly understand what’s happening in the business. Among all Dynamics 365 customizations, reporting and dashboard improvements are often some of the most valuable because they help organizations get more insight from the data they’re already collecting.

Custom Fields With a Clear Purpose

Custom fields aren’t the enemy. The key question is why the field exists. If it supports reporting, forecasting, automation, or a business process, it may be worthwhile. If there’s no clear answer, it’s probably worth reconsidering.

Which customizations should you avoid?

Five tend to cause more problems than they solve: fields added just in case, a rebuild of your old CRM, customizing around a broken process, complex code without a business case, and approvals for everything.

Adding Fields “Just in Case”

Most CRM administrators have heard this request: “Let’s add the field now in case we need it later.”

Unfortunately, “just in case” fields have a way of multiplying. Over time, they clutter forms, confuse users, and make data entry more frustrating.

Recreating Your Old CRM

One of the biggest mistakes enCloud9 sees is treating Dynamics 365 as an opportunity to rebuild an old CRM system feature-for-feature. A new CRM implementation should improve processes, not preserve every habit from the past. Often, the most effective Dynamics 365 customizations simplify the user experience rather than replicate legacy systems.

Customizing Around a Broken Process

Technology can’t fix a broken process. Before requesting new Dynamics 365 customizations, ask whether the underlying process is working. Otherwise, you may end up automating inefficiencies instead of solving them.

Complex Custom Code Without a Strong Business Case

Custom code has its place, but it comes with long-term maintenance costs. Whenever standard functionality, configuration, or low-code tools can meet the requirement, that’s often the better long-term choice. Every custom development project should have a clear business justification.

Approval Processes for Everything

Approvals can improve accountability, but they can also create bottlenecks. enCloud9 has seen organizations build complex approval chains that slow down day-to-day work and frustrate users. The goal should be control where it’s needed, not approval for every single action.

How do you decide before building one?

Before approving any Dynamics 365 customization, ask:

  • What business problem does this solve?
  • How many users will benefit?
  • Can standard functionality accomplish the same thing?
  • Who will maintain it over time?
  • Will this still make sense three years from now?

If those questions are difficult to answer, the customization may not be necessary.

The Bottom Line on Dynamics 365 Customizations

The best Dynamics 365 environments aren’t usually the most customized. They’re the ones where every field, workflow, form, integration, and report serves a clear purpose.

enCloud9 has worked with organizations that struggled because they didn’t customize enough, and with many more that struggled because years of well-intentioned Dynamics 365 customizations created systems that were harder to use, harder to maintain, and harder to trust.

The goal isn’t to avoid Dynamics 365 customizations. The goal is to make thoughtful decisions that improve the user experience, support business goals, and keep the system manageable as your organization grows.

Further Reading

If you’re evaluating your Dynamics 365 environment, these resources may also help:

  • Tension Envelope: a stalled Dynamics 365 project, brought to life: how enCloud9 restarted a project a prior partner left stalled, within three months.
  • Why Your Dynamics 365 CRM Feels Like Extra Work Instead of a Helpful Tool: signs that your CRM may be creating friction instead of helping employees be more productive.
  • Is Your Dynamics 365 Healthy or Just “Working?”: how to identify CRM drift before it impacts adoption, reporting, and business performance.

Need Help Deciding Which Dynamics 365 Customizations Are Worth Keeping?

If your Dynamics 365 environment has grown more complicated over the years, you’re not alone. enCloud9 has worked with organizations that have accumulated years of fields, workflows, reports, and customizations, many of which no longer serve a clear purpose.

Whether you’re evaluating a new request, planning a cleanup project, or simply wondering if your CRM has become more complex than it needs to be, enCloud9 can help. enCloud9 helps you identify what’s adding value, what’s creating unnecessary complexity, and where opportunities exist to simplify and optimize your system.

enCloud9 focuses on Dynamics 365 and works with a network of Business Central partners for the accounting setup. enCloud9 connects the two systems so they work as one.

What kinds of Dynamics 365 licenses are there?

LicenseWho it is forWhat to know

What is a Dynamics 365 attach license?

An attach license adds a second app to a user who already has a base license, at a lower price than a full license. The base must be the highest-priced app that user needs.

What can a Team Members user do?

View records, enter time and expenses, and update their own items through Microsoft's Team Member apps, which can be customized with up to 15 extra tables. Team Members does not cover custom apps. If a Team Members user starts doing full work, Microsoft expects a full license.

Not for apps that extend their licensed Dynamics 365 app in the same environment. Apps used outside that context need Power Apps licensing, and Microsoft enforces this more strictly from February 2027.

What happens if we run out of storage?

Microsoft is rolling out stricter storage checks: past 100%, creating, copying and restoring environments is blocked; after 30 days sandboxes go admin-only, and after 90 days sign-in to them is blocked. Production environments are not locked. Today Microsoft sends email warnings.

No. Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits are not part of the package price, and you pay for them separately. As part of the build we assign your licenses to each user and set their security roles, because Microsoft does not let a user open the app until both are done.

Is the Sales Accelerator the same as the sales accelerator in Dynamics 365?

No. Microsoft's sales accelerator is a feature inside Dynamics 365 Sales that gives sellers a prioritized work list and sequences of follow-up steps. Our Sales Accelerator is a package: we build Dynamics 365 Sales for your team to a fixed scope.

Do we need Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium?

Most B2B sales teams start with Sales Enterprise, because it adds Copilot, forecasting and territory management to the core CRM. Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.

Can you move our data from Salesforce, HubSpot or spreadsheets?

Yes. Yes. The Sales Accelerator imports up to 500 records from one source. Data from several systems is part of a full implementation. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.

What if we need more than the package covers?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. If you need integrations or data from several systems at go-live, a full implementation fits better.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.

The Sales Accelerator takes 4 weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. The Schiff Group went live on a new Dynamics 365 Sales system in one month.

Do we need Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium?

Most B2B sales teams start with Sales Enterprise, because it adds Copilot, forecasting and territory management to the core CRM. Professional suits small teams that need core pipeline tracking without Copilot. Premium suits teams that plan to run agents at volume, since it includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user per month.

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.

What do the Sales agents cost to run?

Agents use Copilot Credits for each answer and action. Microsoft sells credits in packs of 25,000 for $200 a month, or pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription. We estimate your monthly use with Microsoft's estimator and set a spending limit before an agent goes live.

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 Sales system another partner built?

Yes. Our Rescue and Repair package takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can. Tension Envelope's stalled project from a prior partner was back on track within three months.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, from 7:00am to 5:00pm Central.

Can you move our data from Salesforce, HubSpot or spreadsheets?

Yes. Moving data from your old CRM or spreadsheets is part of a full implementation, and the Sales Accelerator includes an import of up to 500 records. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.

Home/Packages and support/Rescue and Repair
Package 02 · Rescue and Repair

Dynamics 365 Rescue and Repair

Rescue and Repair takes over a Dynamics 365 system that is over-customized, stalled with another partner or out of date, and gets it working again. enCloud9 reviews it first and tells you what to keep, then takes it back to standard features where it can. It runs $500 to $10,000, typically 8 to 16 weeks for a full rescue. Microsoft licenses are separate.

Book a call Free checkups, no obligation →

Prefer the phone? Call 1-844-264-0729.

Price

Time

First step

3 monthsA stalled Dynamics 365 Sales project from a prior partner, back on track for Tension EnvelopeRead the story →
11 of 23of our client stories start from a Dynamics system that was failing or out of date
23client stories, new builds to rescuesSee the stories → $500a month, where support plans startSee support plans →

What does Rescue and Repair include?

Rescue and Repair covers what your review finds and your signed scope names: removing customizations you do not need, finishing what stalled, cleaning your data and, if needed, moving an on-premises system to the cloud. New integrations, agents and Microsoft licenses are not part of it.

Included

  • A review of your current system, with a written list of what to keep, fix or remove
  • Unneeded customizations removed and standard features put back where they fit
  • A stalled project finished to a written plan
  • Duplicate records cleaned up
  • An on-premises Dynamics system moved to the cloud, if in scope
  • Training on the repaired system and handover to a support plan

Not included

  • Anything not named in the signed scope
  • New integrations and agents, scoped separately
  • Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts.

Want to know what your system needs?Book a call

Is Rescue and Repair right for your business?

Rescue and Repair fits a business that already runs Dynamics 365 or an older Dynamics CRM and cannot get it to work. If this is your first Dynamics 365 system, an accelerator or a full implementation fits better.

Not sure? Book a call and we will tell you which package fits.

Book a call

A good fit if

  • Your Dynamics 365 system is so customized that your team works around it.
  • Your Dynamics 365 project stalled with another partner.
  • You still run an on-premises Dynamics CRM.
  • Your records have duplicates and nobody trusts the reports.

Consider another option if

  • This is your first Dynamics 365 system. The Sales Accelerator or Service Accelerator is built for that.
  • You are moving to Dynamics 365 with data from several systems. A full implementation is built for that.
  • Your system works and you want ongoing help each month. A support plan is built for that.

How does a Dynamics 365 rescue run?

Every rescue runs through four stages: Review, Repair, Go live and Run. You see the written list of what we keep, fix or remove before we change anything, and every change after that is written down and approved.

Stage AReviewWe review your system, your customizations and your data, and give you a written list of what to keep, fix or remove, with a written quote.
Stage BRepairWe take the system back to standard features where they fit, finish what stalled and clean your data. You check the records before sign-off.
Stage CGo liveTraining on the repaired system and cut-over day. New agents are scoped separately.
Stage DRunYour support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed.

Which Dynamics systems have we rescued?

Here are three of our 23 client stories, each starting from a Dynamics system that was not working: one set up without professional guidance, one stalled with a prior partner and one out of date.

Des Moines, IA · Product: Dynamics 365 · Rescue and RepairRescuedAureonA Dynamics CRM set up without professional guidance, underused and unreliable. enCloud9 audited it and built an enhancement plan; for the first time, staff can rely on Dynamics 365.Read the Aureon story → Kansas City, MO · Product: Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise · Timeline: within three months3 monthsTension EnvelopeA stalled project from a prior partner, back on track within three months.Read the Tension Envelope story → Peculiar, MO · Product: Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise · Timeline: 3 to 4 months3 to 4 monthsElmwood Reclaimed TimberAn on-premises Dynamics system moved to the cloud within 3 to 4 months.Read the Elmwood story →
All 23 client stories →

What does support cost after go-live?

Support starts at $500 a month for 4 hours on the Stability plan, which is the minimum plan for new clients. Larger teams choose Optimization at $1,500 a month for 20 hours or Partnership from $2,000 a month for 35 hours.

HourlyOn-Demand$200an hourAs needed, no retainer. Anyone can ask. No SLA.Compare support plans → Minimum planStability$500a month4 hours a month.Compare support plans → Monthly planOptimization$1,500a month20 hours a month. Up to 50 users.Compare support plans → Monthly planPartnership$2,000a month35 hours a month. 50 users and up.Compare support plans →

Monthly plans run on a 12-month agreement. New clients pay an onboarding fee of up to one month's charge. Hours 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, which means a person has picked up your request, not that it is solved. Every monthly plan includes Microsoft escalation management.

Compare support plans

Rescue and Repair questions

Something else on your mind? Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.

Book a call1-844-264-0729 →
How much does Dynamics 365 Rescue and Repair cost?

Rescue and Repair runs from $500 for a small fix to $10,000, quoted in writing after we review your system, because every system breaks differently. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.

How long does a Dynamics 365 rescue take?

A full rescue typically takes 8 to 16 weeks. You get the plan, with dates, before we change anything. Tension Envelope was back on track within three months, and Elmwood Reclaimed Timber moved from on-premises to the cloud within 3 to 4 months.

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 system another partner built?

Yes. Rescue and Repair takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can. Tension Envelope's stalled project from a prior partner was back on track within three months.

Do we have to start over?

No. Rescue and Repair is for Dynamics 365 systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date. We review it first and tell you what to keep.

Can you move our on-premises Dynamics CRM to the cloud?

Yes. Moving an on-premises Dynamics system to Dynamics 365 in the cloud can be part of the scope. Elmwood Reclaimed Timber moved its on-premises system to the cloud within 3 to 4 months.

Are Microsoft licenses included?

No. Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits are not part of the package price, and you pay for them separately. As part of the repair we check each user has the right license and security role, because Microsoft does not let a user open the app until both are done.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.

Our accelerators are fixed-scope packages for a first Dynamics 365 system. You see the scope, price and timeline in writing before we start, and anything outside the package is a written change order you approve first.

The Sales Accelerator is for a team that sells through stages, quotes or products and is starting on Dynamics 365 Sales. The Service Accelerator is for a team that handles customer requests and is starting on Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

Each accelerator is a fixed $7,500 for our build work. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.

Is the Sales Accelerator the same as the sales accelerator in Dynamics 365?

No. Microsoft's sales accelerator is a feature inside Dynamics 365 Sales that gives sellers a prioritized work list and sequences of follow-up steps. Our Sales Accelerator is a package: we build Dynamics 365 Sales for your team to a fixed scope.

Home/Questions
Questions · All topics

Questions, answered

This page holds every question from our product, package and company pages, 205 in all, grouped by topic. Each answer links back to the page it comes from. Search the list, or jump to a topic: Dynamics 365, Copilot and AI, marketing, packages, moving from another CRM, and support.

Book a call

205 questions

Getting started (41)Dynamics 365 (49)Copilot, AI and Power Platform (41)Marketing and email (11)Packages (24)Moving to Dynamics 365 (16)Support and storage (23)

Getting started

41 questions

How much does Dynamics 365 cost?

Microsoft list prices for Dynamics 365 Sales are $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly. Sales and Service Accelerators are $7,500, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each quoted in writing. Support starts at $500 a month. See our pricing guide.From Home →

How long does a Dynamics 365 setup take?

Our accelerators take 4 weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Home →

Can you take over a system another partner built?

Yes. Rescue and Repair is for Dynamics 365 systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date. We review it first and tell you what to keep.From Home →

Is Copilot included with Dynamics 365?

Copilot is built into Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise and Premium. Agents run on Copilot Credits, which most plans buy separately. We tell you what it costs to run before anything is switched on.From Home →

What is a generative page?

A page in your Dynamics 365 app that is built from a plain-words request, such as a report on deals that have gone quiet. It runs inside your Dynamics 365 app, on your live records.From Home →

What happens on the first call?

You tell us where your system is today and what is not working. You get a straight answer on what fits, whether or not you work with us.From Contact us →

Is the first call free?

Yes. The first call is free, with no obligation.From Contact us →

Where is enCloud9 located?

Our office is at 2915 Lynnwood Dr., Bellevue, NE 68123. We work with clients across the US.From Contact us →

How fast do you reply?

We reply within one business day. For a quicker answer, call 1-844-264-0729.From Contact us →

I am already a client. How do I get help?

Call 1-844-264-0729 or see our support plans.From Contact us →

Is enCloud9 based in Omaha?

Yes. Our office is at 2915 Lynnwood Dr., Bellevue, NE 68123, in the Omaha metro. We work with clients in Nebraska, Iowa and across the US.From Omaha and Nebraska →

Do you work on site or remotely?

Mostly remotely, through Teams and screen sharing. For Omaha-area clients, we visit on site when the work needs it.From Omaha and Nebraska →

What Dynamics 365 work do you do?

We build new Dynamics 365 systems, rescue ones that are not working, run fixed-scope accelerators for Sales and Customer Service, and support systems after go-live.From Omaha and Nebraska →

How long does a Dynamics 365 project take?

A full implementation or a Rescue and Repair usually takes 8 to 16 weeks and is quoted for your project. A fixed-scope accelerator is shorter.From Omaha and Nebraska →

How long have you worked with your clients?

enCloud9 has been a Microsoft Partner since 2008. Clinical Reference Lab (CRL) has been a client for more than 15 years.From Omaha and Nebraska →

Do you have Omaha clients?

Yes. One is Radio Engineering Industries in Omaha, which runs its five divisions on Dynamics 365.From Omaha and Nebraska →

What do we get in writing before you start?

A written plan with the scope and the timeline. The price for our build work is fixed for an accelerator and quoted for a full implementation or Rescue and Repair. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost.From How we work →

What if we need something the plan does not cover?

Anything outside the plan is a written change order you approve before work starts.From How we work →

Who will we work with?

[Brian confirms: who leads a project and who does the build work.]From How we work →

How often will we hear from you during a project?

[Brian confirms: the regular check-in during a project.]From How we work →

What happens after go-live?

Your support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed. Plans start at $500 a month for 4 hours.From How we work →

Who will work on our project?

[Brian confirms: who leads a project and who does the build work.]From Team →

Where is the team?

Our office is in Bellevue, Nebraska, in the Omaha metro. We work with clients across the US, mostly remotely.From Team →

Is Dynamics 365 HIPAA compliant?

Microsoft includes Dynamics 365 in its HIPAA Business Associate Agreement. Using it does not make you compliant on its own; your setup, access rules and processes have to meet HIPAA too.From Healthcare →

How do we get a BAA from Microsoft?

Microsoft makes its HIPAA Business Associate Agreement available by default through its Data Protection Addendum to customers who are covered entities or business associates.From Healthcare →

Does enCloud9 sign a BAA with clients?

[Brian confirms.]From Healthcare →

Which Dynamics 365 apps do healthcare clients use?

Our healthcare clients run Dynamics 365 Sales, and PriceMDs adds Customer Service. Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI extend them on the same data.From Healthcare →

Can you fix a healthcare CRM another partner built?

Yes. enCloud9 takes over systems other partners built, finds what is broken, and fixes it in priority order. See Rescue and Repair.From Healthcare →

Do you work with professional services firms?

Yes. Our clients include a government contracting consultancy, a business support services firm and a private equity firm, and CRM Software Blog listed us as its Professional Services partner on its 2026 list.From Professional services →

Which Dynamics 365 app does a professional services firm need?

Most start with Dynamics 365 Sales for clients, contacts and pipeline. Firms that run projects, track time and bill for it add Project Operations.From Professional services →

How long does it take? (Professional services)

A full implementation or a Rescue and Repair usually runs 8 to 16 weeks and is quoted for your project. The Schiff Group moved to Dynamics 365 Sales in one month.From Professional services →

Can you fix a CRM we already have?

Yes. Aureon had a Dynamics CRM set up without professional help; we audited it, reviewed its processes and built the plan to fix it. See Rescue and Repair.From Professional services →

What does it cost? (Professional services)

Sales and Service Accelerators are $7,500 fixed, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each quoted in writing. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.From Professional services →

Do you work with manufacturers?

Yes. Our clients include makers of bus safety systems, analytical instruments, flexible packaging, envelopes, packaging equipment and wastewater equipment.From Manufacturing →

Can Dynamics 365 handle several divisions?

Yes. For REI we built sales processes for five divisions in one Dynamics 365 system, with dashboards that show management the sales trends.From Manufacturing →

Can you connect Dynamics 365 to our other systems?

Yes. For Tension Envelope we connected Dynamics 365 to its data warehouse, and for JWC Environmental we connected web leads to Dynamics 365 with automatic assignment.From Manufacturing →

What about our ERP?

Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service handle the customer side. If you run Business Central, see the Business Central integration. For another ERP, tell us what you run and we will tell you what the link takes.From Manufacturing →

Do you work with distributors?

Yes. enCloud9 builds Dynamics 365 for small and mid-sized businesses, and distributors are one of the industries we lead with.From Distribution →

Can our sellers see stock and credit in Dynamics 365?

Yes, if you run Business Central. Microsoft's integration shows item availability, price lists, balances and open invoices in Dynamics 365 Sales. See the Business Central integration.From Distribution →

What if we run a different ERP?

Tell us what you run and we will tell you what the link takes. Other connections can be built with Power Automate or custom work, quoted in writing.From Distribution →

Can Dynamics 365 handle returns?

Yes. Dynamics 365 Customer Service tracks each return or question as a case, with queues and service levels, so nothing sits in one inbox.From Distribution →

Dynamics 365

Which Dynamics 365 app do I need?

Pick the app that matches the work you want to fix first: selling, service, phone and chat, field visits, marketing or projects. Most growing businesses start with Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service or both, and add the others when the work calls for them.From Dynamics 365 →

Can one person use two Dynamics 365 apps?

Yes. Each full user gets one base license for the highest-priced app they need, plus a lower-priced attach license for each extra app. People who only read records or enter time can use the lower-cost Team Members license.From Dynamics 365 →

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.From Dynamics 365 →

How much does Dynamics 365 Sales cost?

Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Setup is a separate project, quoted in writing after a short call, and support plans start at $500 a month. Agents can add Copilot Credit costs, which we estimate before you switch them on.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

How long does a Dynamics 365 Sales implementation take?

The Sales Accelerator takes 4 weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. The Schiff Group went live on a new Dynamics 365 Sales system in one month.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Do we need Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium?

Most B2B sales teams start with Sales Enterprise, because it adds Copilot, forecasting and territory management to the core CRM. Professional suits small teams that need core pipeline tracking without Copilot. Premium suits teams that plan to run agents at volume, since it includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user per month.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

What do the Sales agents cost to run?

Agents use Copilot Credits for each answer and action. Microsoft sells credits in packs of 25,000 for $200 a month, or pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription. We estimate your monthly use with Microsoft's estimator and set a spending limit before an agent goes live.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 Sales system another partner built?

Yes. Our Rescue and Repair package takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can. Tension Envelope's stalled project from a prior partner was back on track within three months.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Can you move our data from Salesforce, HubSpot or spreadsheets?

Yes. Moving data from your old CRM or spreadsheets is part of a full implementation, and the Sales Accelerator includes an import of up to 500 records. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

How much does Dynamics 365 Customer Service cost?

Microsoft's list price is $50, $105 or $195 per user per month, paid yearly, for Customer Service Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Setup is a separate project, quoted in writing after a short call, and support plans start at $500 a month. Agents can add Copilot Credit costs, which we estimate before you switch them on.From Customer Service →

How long does a Dynamics 365 Customer Service implementation take?

What messages will we see from Microsoft?

Warning emails, plus banners in the Power Platform admin center, the maker portals and your Dynamics 365 apps. They start when less than 15% of your database, file or log storage is left, get stronger below 5%, and continue once you are over. Admins and makers get the emails every week.From Dataverse storage →

Will Dynamics 365 CRM stop working?

How much does extra Dataverse storage cost?

Should we buy more storage or clean up our data?

It depends which storage type is over and what is using it. Database storage is expensive, so a cleanup often pays for itself. The analysis recommends one or both.From Dataverse storage →

What takes up the most Dataverse storage?

Usually old emails and attachments, notes, audit history, system logs and environments nobody uses. The analysis finds the biggest tables and the fastest-growing ones.From Dataverse storage →

How Microsoft Updates Dynamics 365 Now

Guide

By Brian Begley[publish date]4 min read

At a glance

  • Published[publish date]
  • TopicGuide
  • Reading time4 minutes
  • Written byBrian Begley
On this page
  1. What changed when Microsoft retired release waves?
  2. How often does Dynamics 365 get updated?
  3. What are the monthly and semi-annual release channels?
  4. Do the April and October releases still happen?
  5. Can you test new features before they reach production?
  6. Where do you find what is coming next?
  7. What does this mean for your Dynamics 365 system?
  8. Frequently asked questions
  9. Want someone to watch the updates for you?

The short answerMicrosoft stopped publishing twice-yearly release plans for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform in September 2026. Upcoming features now appear on the AI at Work roadmap on a rolling basis. Updates still ship weekly. Model-driven apps switch on new features every month, or twice a year in April and October, depending on the release channel.

Checked 10 November 2026

When was this page checked?

Every Microsoft fact on this page links to the Microsoft page it came from, checked 10 November 2026. enCloud9 rechecks it each month with the monthly Dynamics 365 roundup.

Microsoft announced the change to partners on 4 September 2026, in the notice linked below.

What changed when Microsoft retired release waves?

Microsoft stopped announcing features in two big release waves a year. Its September 2026 notice to partners says (checked 10 November 2026):

  • Roadmap content for Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Dataverse moves to the AI at Work roadmap.
  • Microsoft is moving from twice-yearly release waves to continuous roadmap and change communications.
  • There is no September 2026 Release Wave 2 announcement.
  • Microsoft is archiving release plans on Microsoft Learn and retiring Release Planner by November 15, 2026.
  • Roadmap items with public preview or general availability dates on or after June 1, 2026 are expected to move to the new roadmap.

What did not change: Microsoft says this affects roadmap communications only. Release schedules, deployment processes, Message Center notices and product documentation stay the same.

How often does Dynamics 365 get updated?

Every week. Microsoft delivers security and minor service improvements weekly, rolling out region by region on a safe deployment schedule (checked 10 November 2026).

  • Each weekly update starts in Microsoft’s “First Release” region.
  • A Message Center notice gives the date the deployment begins.
  • Your environment updates later, during your region’s maintenance window. In North America that window is 2 AM to 11 AM UTC.
  • To check what you have, open the environment’s About page and read the version number.

What are the monthly and semi-annual release channels?

Release channels decide how often people see new, generally available features in model-driven apps (checked 10 November 2026).

Monthly channel

New features switch on once a month, with about a week’s notice to admins. A release reaches all regions over roughly five weeks. When the setting is Auto, environments use this channel.

Semi-annual channel

New features switch on twice a year, starting in early April and early October. Microsoft suggests it for teams that need more training and testing before a change.

Both channels deliver generally available features only. Security and non-user-facing changes still arrive with the weekly updates on either channel.

Do the April and October releases still happen?

Yes. Power Platform still has two major releases each year, in April and October, and you can’t postpone them (checked 10 November 2026).

The October 2026 release reached North America on October 23 to 26, 2026, with database version 9.2.26093. Microsoft posts the dates for each region in Message Center.

Can you test new features before they reach production?

Yes, with early access, but the switch is being rebuilt. Microsoft removed the Early Access switch before the April 2026 release and plans to bring it back later in 2026 (checked 10 November 2026).

  • On the monthly channel, early access gives about two weeks to validate.
  • On the semi-annual channel, it gives about seven weeks.
  • Microsoft recommends a sandbox copy of production, on the same release channel as production.

Where do you find what is coming next?

  • The AI at Work roadmap, formerly the Microsoft 365 Roadmap. You can filter it, export to CSV and subscribe by RSS.
  • Message Center in the Microsoft 365 admin center, for dates that affect your tenant.
  • Microsoft’s release schedules page, which links the update guidance for each app, such as version histories and early access.
  • enCloud9’s monthly roundup, with every item linked to Microsoft.

What does this mean for your Dynamics 365 system?

Plan for small, steady changes instead of two big ones a year. enCloud9 suggests four habits, each based on Microsoft’s own guidance above:

  • Pick a release channel on purpose, and keep development, test and production on the same one.
  • Read Message Center notices weekly, or have someone do it for you.
  • Test changes in a sandbox copy of production before they reach users.
  • Check the AI at Work roadmap each month for the apps you use.

If you would rather hand this off, enCloud9’s support plans start at $500 a month.

Frequently asked questions

Did Microsoft stop the April and October updates?

No. Microsoft stopped publishing release plans and twice-yearly release wave announcements. Power Platform still has major releases in April and October, and you can’t postpone them.

Where are the old release plans?

Microsoft is archiving them on Microsoft Learn for reference and retiring Release Planner by November 15, 2026.

Which release channel does a new environment use?

When the setting is Auto, Power Platform and Dynamics 365 environments use the Monthly channel. Admins can choose Semi-annual for a slower pace.

Free Dataverse Storage Analysis

Getting Dataverse storage warnings from Microsoft?

You need a plan before the restrictions start. Don't just buy more Dataverse storage. Buy the right Dataverse storage.

Once Dataverse storage passes 85%, Microsoft emails your admins every week. It is now rolling out limits that block environment copies and restores, then lock sandboxes, when you go over. Book my free storage analysis

Concept only: nothing is sent from this page. On the live site this is the same ClickDimensions form as today.

Microsoft's four steps

Don't ignore it: four steps from warning to lockout

Microsoft is rolling out staged limits for Dataverse storage. Today only the warning emails are on. Once the rollout reaches your tenant, here is what happens when you go over.

  1. 85%Past 85%The warnings start. Once you are near or over the limit, your admins get them every week, with no way to switch them off.
  2. 100%The day you go overYou cannot create, copy, restore or recover environments. That includes restoring an environment from a backup if something goes wrong.
  3. 30 days30 days overYour sandbox environments lock to administrators only.
  4. 90 days90 days overNobody can sign in to those sandboxes, admins included.

Your production apps keep running, but anything that needs a restore, a copy or a test environment is blocked.

Source: Microsoft, "Dataverse capacity-based storage details" (read 6 November 2026). The staged limits apply to Dataverse-only tenants as Microsoft rolls out its new storage validation; sandboxes on pay-as-you-go billing are not locked.

Database, file and log

Three kinds of Dataverse storage, three different bills

Dataverse storage splits three ways. Which one is over decides the fix and the cost.

01 · DatabaseYour recordsAccounts, contacts, opportunities and the rest.The most expensive. Every extra GB can cost up to $500 a year.
02 · FileYour documents and attachmentsThe more emails you track into Dataverse, the larger this one grows.
03 · LogAudit history and system jobsIt can fill up surprisingly quickly if you have user access auditing turned on.
Two ways out

Two solutions to Dataverse storage problems

1Buy more storage.It works, but every extra GB of database storage can cost up to $500 a year, and you keep paying it every year.
2Clean up what you don't need.We show you exactly which tables, attachments, logs and old environments are using your space, then delete or archive what you don't need, safely.

The enCloud9 Dataverse Storage Analysis tells you exactly which one you need, or how much of each.

  4. The tables using the most space, and the ones growing fastest.
  5. A written recommendation: buy more, clean up, or both.
  6. A plan to get back under your limit and stay there.
Questions we hear

Dataverse storage questions

Still not sure where you stand? The analysis answers these for your own tenant.

Book my free storage analysis
What happens when we go over our Dataverse storage limit?

Once Microsoft's rollout reaches your tenant: from the day you go over, you cannot create, copy, restore or recover environments. After 30 days, sandbox environments are limited to administrators. After 90 days, nobody can sign in to them, admins included.

What messages will we see from Microsoft?

Warning emails, plus banners in the Power Platform admin center, the maker portals and your Dynamics 365 apps. They start when less than 15% of your database, file or log storage is left, get stronger below 5%, and continue once you are over. Admins and makers get the emails every week.

Will Dynamics 365 CRM stop working?

No. Your production apps keep running. What is blocked is anything that needs a restore, a copy or a test environment.

Can we turn off Microsoft's storage warning emails or notifications?

No. Once you are near or over the limit, admins get the emails every week, with no way to opt out. A banner you dismiss stays hidden for seven days, then comes back if you are still over.

Which storage type is my warning about?

Dataverse storage splits into database, file and log. You can see the split in the Power Platform admin center under Licensing, then Dataverse. The free analysis checks this for you.

How much does extra Dataverse storage cost?

Extra database storage can cost up to $500 per GB a year.

Should we buy more storage or clean up our data?

It depends which storage type is over and what is using it. Database storage is expensive, so a cleanup often pays for itself. The analysis recommends one or both.

What takes up the most Dataverse storage?

Usually old emails and attachments, notes, audit history, system logs and environments nobody uses. The analysis finds the biggest tables and the fastest-growing ones.
