Move · Move from HubSpot

Move from HubSpot to Dynamics 365 Sales

enCloud9 moves growing US businesses from HubSpot to Dynamics 365 Sales: your contacts, companies, deals, pipelines and history, with record counts checked against HubSpot before go-live. A move is part of a full implementation, quoted after a short call. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.

Book a call Get the migration checklist →

Prefer the phone? Call 1-844-264-0729.

ReviewedYour portalA written review of your HubSpot portal↘︎ MappedObjects and propertiesHubSpot objects and properties mapped to Dynamics 365 Sales↘︎ MappedUsers and rolesHubSpot users mapped to Dynamics 365 users and security roles↘︎ AssignedLicensesYour Microsoft licenses assigned to each user↘︎ MoveFrom HubSpotYour HubSpot data moved to Dynamics 365 Sales TestedTrial runA trial run first, then the full move↘︎ CheckedRecord countsUp to [Brian sets] records moved, counts checked against HubSpot↘︎ Stage CTraining[Brian sets] training sessions↘︎ After go-liveHelp[Brian sets] days of help after go-live↘︎

Microsoft licenses are not part of the package price. Microsoft's list price for Dynamics 365 Sales is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly.

$65a user a month, Microsoft's lowest Dynamics 365 Sales list priceCompare list prices → 4stages: Plan, Build, Go live and RunHow a move runs → 23client stories, new builds to rescuesSee the stories → $500a month, where support plans startSee support plans →

No published enCloud9 story measures a move from HubSpot yet.

What moves from HubSpot to Dynamics 365?

Your HubSpot contacts, companies, deals, pipelines and activity history move to Dynamics 365 Sales, mapped field by field and tested in a trial run before the full move. HubSpot workflows, sequences and connected apps do not move on their own; enCloud9 reviews them first and quotes any rebuild separately.

Included

  • A written review of your HubSpot portal: objects, properties, pipelines, workflows and connected apps
  • Your HubSpot objects and properties mapped to Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Your HubSpot users mapped to Dynamics 365 users and security roles
  • Your Microsoft licenses assigned to each user
  • A trial run first, then the full move, with record counts checked against HubSpot
  • Up to [Brian sets] records moved
  • [Brian sets] training sessions
  • [Brian sets] days of help after go-live

Not included

  • Rebuilding HubSpot workflows, sequences and connected apps, quoted separately
  • Marketing Hub emails, forms and landing pages, quoted separately
  • Integrations with other systems, quoted separately
  • Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits
  • Ending your HubSpot contract, which stays between you and HubSpot

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. Want to know what your portal would take? Book a call.

Ask about a move from HubSpot

What do Dynamics 365 Sales and HubSpot Sales Hub cost per user?

Microsoft lists Dynamics 365 Sales at $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly. HubSpot lists Sales Hub Starter from $7, Professional from $90 and Enterprise from $150 per seat per month, plus a one-time onboarding fee of $1,500 for Professional and $3,500 for Enterprise.

List prices per user per month, from each vendor's own pricing page
EditionList price per user per monthBillingOne-time onboarding fee

List prices from each vendor's own pricing page, Salesforce, HubSpot and Microsoft read 10 Nov 2026; we check them again before this page goes live. Editions do not line up feature for feature, so compare the edition you use today with the plan you need. Neither price includes setup or support.

HubSpot's paid prices are the lowest "starts at" prices it shows, and it also has a free plan for up to 2 users. Its page also shows higher prices for Starter and Professional, and some discounts are for new customers only.

Who moves from HubSpot to Dynamics 365?

A move fits a sales team on HubSpot whose setup is mostly standard records, such as contacts, companies and deals, and who already work in Outlook and Teams.

Not sure? Book a call and enCloud9 will tell you which package fits.

Book a call

Moves go smoothest when

  • Your team already works in Outlook and Teams every day.
  • You sell through a sales process with stages, quotes or products.
  • Most of your HubSpot setup is standard records: contacts, companies and deals.
  • Your HubSpot renewal date is coming and you want a plan before it arrives.

Consider another option if

  • You need other systems connected on day one. Those integrations are quoted on top of the move, inside the same full implementation.
  • You have one or two people who only need shared contacts. The Sales Accelerator is a smaller start.

How does a move from HubSpot run?

Every project runs through the same four stages: Plan, Build, Go live and Run. You see the written plan before we build, and every change after that is written down and approved.

Stage APlanenCloud9 learns how you sell, using a written discovery questionnaire, and gives you the plan: users, sales stages, data to move, integrations, and where Copilot and agents fit.
Stage BBuildenCloud9 builds Dynamics 365 Sales to the plan, using standard features first, and moves your data. You check the imported records against your old system before sign-off.
Stage CGo liveTraining and cut-over day. Copilot is switched on if your plan includes it; agents are scoped as a separate pilot.
Stage DRunYour support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed.

What does support cost after go-live?

Support starts at $500 a month for 4 hours on the Stability plan, which is the minimum plan for new clients. Larger teams choose Optimization at $1,500 a month for 20 hours or Partnership from $2,000 a month for 35 hours.

HourlyOn-Demand$200an hourAs needed, no retainer. Anyone can ask. Up to 50 users.Compare support plans → Monthly planPartnershipFrom$2,000a month35 hours a month. 50 users and up.Compare support plans →

Monthly plans run on a 12-month agreement. New clients pay an onboarding fee of up to one month's charge. Hours 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, which means a person has picked up your request, not that it is solved. Every monthly plan includes Microsoft escalation management.

HubSpot move questions

Book a call1-844-264-0729 →
How much does a move from HubSpot cost?

A move from HubSpot is part of a full implementation: from $20,000, quoted after a short call, usually 8 to 16 weeks. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.

How long does a move from HubSpot take?

A move usually takes 8 to 16 weeks, as part of a full implementation. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.

Do our HubSpot workflows and sequences move across?

Not on their own. Workflows, sequences and connected apps are rebuilt in Dynamics 365 rather than copied. enCloud9 reviews them first and quotes any rebuild separately.

Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from HubSpot?

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.

Are Microsoft licenses included?

No. Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits are not part of the package price, and you pay for them separately. As part of the move, enCloud9 assigns your licenses to each user and sets their security roles. Microsoft does not let a user open the app until both are done.

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales and the basic Sales agent in Outlook and Teams are included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. Premium Sales agent features need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.

What if we need more than the package covers?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. Integrations and data from other systems are quoted inside the full implementation.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.

Copilot and AI for Dynamics 365

Put Copilot and agents to work on your Dynamics 365 data

AI in Dynamics 365 comes in three forms: Copilot inside the app, agents Microsoft includes, and agents built for your business in Copilot Studio. enCloud9 builds each one after a data and permissions review and gives you the running cost first. Compana Pet Brands runs a Copilot Studio agent that enCloud9 built and put into production.

Book a call Free checkups, no obligation →

Prefer the phone? Call 1-844-264-0729.

AppDynamics 365 SalesSummaries, email drafts and meeting prep, inside the appCopilot in Enterprise and Premium↗︎ Agent, SalesSales Qualification AgentResearches leads and drafts outreachGenerally available↗︎ Agent, SalesSales Opportunity AgentFlags deal risks and shows which deals to focus onGenerally available↗︎ Built for youCopilot Studio agentsFor a job only your business hasQuoted in writing↗︎ At the centerCopilotOnly sees records the signed-in person can already open PagesGenerative pagesDescribe a screen, get a working pageGenerally available↗︎ AppCustomer ServiceAnswers from your knowledge, drafts replies, summarizes casesCopilot in Enterprise and Premium↗︎ Agent, ServiceCase Management AgentCreates, updates, resolves and closes casesGenerally available↗︎ Agent, ServiceCustomer Intent AgentFinds the most common reasons customers get in touchGenerally available↗︎

Three forms of AI

What are the three forms of AI in Dynamics 365?

Copilot inside the app, agents Microsoft includes with Dynamics 365, and agents built for your business in Copilot Studio. Copilot is included in the Enterprise and Premium plans, while agents run on Copilot Credits. enCloud9 checks your data and permissions and estimates the monthly cost before anything is switched on.

01Copilot in the app02Agents Microsoft includes03Agents built for you Summaries of leads, opportunities and casesLead research and outreach draftsBuilt in Copilot Studio Email and chat reply draftsCases created, updated and closedPublished to Teams or your website
01Copilot in the app Sales. Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales summarizes leads, opportunities and accounts, shows what changed on your records and prepares you for meetings. It also drafts and summarizes emails, answers questions from your SharePoint documents, and brings you news about your accounts. It only sees records the signed-in person can already open. Customer Service. Copilot in Dynamics 365 Customer Service answers your service reps' questions from your own knowledge sources. It summarizes cases and conversations, drafts emails and chat replies, and writes resolution notes. Your reps review every draft before it goes to a customer.
02Agents Microsoft includes Sales. Dynamics 365 Sales includes agents that work on their own: researching leads, watching deals for risk and keeping records up to date. Customer Service. Dynamics 365 Customer Service includes agents that work on their own. They create and update cases, find the most common reasons customers get in touch, turn closed cases into knowledge articles, and score the quality of cases. enCloud9 switches on the ones that fit, tests them on a small group first, and sets a monthly limit on what they can spend.
03Agents built for you For a job only your business has, enCloud9 builds an agent in Copilot Studio that works on your Dynamics 365 data in Dataverse and can be published to Teams or your website. It is quoted in writing, with its running cost written down.
See every agent and its status → Check if your data is ready

Which agents come with Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service?

Microsoft includes agents with both apps. Each one runs on Copilot Credits, and some are still in preview, so enCloud9 tells you which is which before you decide. No client story for Copilot in Sales or Customer Service is shown yet.

Agents in Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service, checked [publish date]
AgentWhat it doesStatus
Dynamics 365 Sales
Sales Qualification AgentResearches assigned leads, checks them against your target customer profile and drafts outreach. In its "research and engage" mode it also emails leads, follows up and hands promising ones to your sellers.Generally available
Sales Opportunity AgentPulls CRM data, email, meetings and web research into one deal view, flags risks and shows which deals to focus on.Generally available
Sales Research AgentAnswers business questions about your pipeline in plain language and builds a research report with charts.[Generally available or preview: confirm the week of publishing]
Recommended Actions AgentRanks the next actions from your other agents into one list for each seller.[Confirm status the week of publishing]
AI-powered Data EnrichmentReads recent customer emails and Teams meetings and suggests updates to opportunities.Generally available
Sales Development agentHandles outreach and prospect follow-up from Microsoft Teams. Needs Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Agent 365.Preview
Dynamics 365 Customer Service
Case Management AgentCreates, updates, resolves, follows up and closes cases. Fully autonomous case resolution needs an application user and a shared mailbox.Generally available
Customer Intent AgentFinds the most common reasons customers get in touch from past and current cases and conversations, and suggests new ones.Generally available
Customer Knowledge Management AgentReads closed cases and drafts or updates knowledge articles to fill gaps.Generally available
Quality Evaluation AgentScores cases against a framework your supervisors set.Generally available
Service AgentLets reps find, summarize and update case information from Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Service workspace.Generally available

Agents run on Copilot Credits. Sales Premium includes 1,000 credits per user per month; other plans buy credits separately. If prepaid credits run out and no pay-as-you-go plan is set, the agents stop until more are added. Microsoft list prices from the Sales and Customer Service pricing pages, checked 10 Nov 2026; they do not include enCloud9’s setup.

Customer Service Premium includes base credit capacity for the four service agents; other plans buy credits separately. Some agents, including the Case Management and Customer Intent agents, also need a pay-as-you-go plan on an Azure subscription.

Preview features are not meant for production use. enCloud9 tells you which is which before you decide.

Generative pages

Describe the screen. Watch the page build.

Generative pages let you describe a screen in plain English and get a working page inside a Dynamics 365 app. Microsoft's app agent writes the code and connects it to your Dataverse tables, and you refine it by chatting. The AI builds the page; the finished page is an ordinary screen on your data.

Pick a request
  1. Describe itSay what the screen should show, in plain English.
  2. The agent builds itMicrosoft's app agent writes the code and connects it to your Dataverse tables.
  3. Refine by chattingAsk for a change and the page updates. Test after each one.

Where do generative pages show up?

  • In the app navigation, as its own page.
  • Inside a form, in a section or tab. The page gets the current record automatically, so you keep the standard form for data entry and add a richer view beside it.
  • Opened from another page or button, with the record passed in.

The AI does its work while the page is being built. The finished page is an ordinary screen that reads and updates your Dynamics 365 records. enCloud9 tests it with your users' real security roles before anyone relies on it.

0additional AI or message credits for the maker experience, Microsoft says. Users still need a license for the app the page sits in.

See it on a call1-844-264-0729 →

When does another tool work better?

  • The job is simple data entry. A standard form is more consistent and easier to support.
  • You need heavy reporting over a lot of data. Use Power BI.
  • People need to ask questions, not open a screen. Copilot in Dynamics 365 answers questions about your data in a side pane.
  • The need is a conversation or an automated process. Build an agent or workflow in Copilot Studio.
  • You need one control reused across many forms. A PCF code component fits better.
  • Several makers must edit the same page at once. Generative pages do not support co-authoring yet.

Also expect to iterate. A new prompt can change parts of the page you were happy with, so test after each change.

How does enCloud9 switch AI on safely?

Nothing is switched on until your data and permissions are ready and the running cost is written down. Every agent goes through the same four steps.

Step 1Data and permissions reviewCopilot only sees records the signed-in person can already open, so we check your security roles, Dataverse search and the quality of your records first.
Step 2A small group firstWe switch on the agents that fit and test them on a small group before the whole team uses them.
Step 3A monthly spend limitWe set a monthly limit on what the agents can spend. If prepaid credits run out and no pay-as-you-go plan is set, the agents stop until more are added.
Step 4Cost estimated before switch-onenCloud9 estimates your monthly use with Microsoft's estimator before an agent goes live, and writes the running cost down.

Copilot and AI questions

Something else on your mind? Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer on what your data is ready for and what it costs to run.

Book a call1-844-264-0729 →
Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Customer Service?

Copilot in Customer Service is included in Customer Service Enterprise and Premium, not in Customer Service Professional. The Case Management, Customer Intent, Customer Knowledge Management and Quality Evaluation agents run on Copilot Credits. Premium includes base Copilot Credit capacity for them; on other plans you buy credits separately. Some agents, including the Case Management and Customer Intent agents, also need a pay-as-you-go plan on an Azure subscription.

What do the Sales agents cost to run?

Agents use Copilot Credits for each answer and action. Microsoft sells credits in packs of 25,000 for $200 a month, or pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription. enCloud9 estimates your monthly use with Microsoft's estimator and sets a spending limit before an agent goes live.

What are generative pages in Dynamics 365?

They are pages in model-driven apps that Microsoft's app agent builds from a plain-language description. The agent writes React code that reads and updates your Dataverse data.

Are generative pages generally available?

Yes. Generative pages in model-driven apps are generally available. Using Power Platform connectors and Dataverse custom APIs with them is still in preview.

Does building generative pages cost extra?

Microsoft says the maker experience doesn't require any additional AI or message credits. Users still need a license for the app the page sits in.

Do generative pages replace Power BI or Copilot?

No. Use Power BI for heavy analytics, Copilot for questions about your data, and generative pages for focused working screens.

When does another tool work better than a generative page?

Simple data entry, big reporting over lots of data, or a chat-style need. enCloud9 will say so before the build and point you to the better tool.

Microsoft's tool for building your own AI agents. An agent answers questions from your data and can take actions, such as creating a case or updating a record.

Dynamics 365 Implementation

An enCloud9 full implementation builds Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service or both, with your data moved from your old systems, the integrations you name and training. It starts at $20,000, typically takes 8 to 16 weeks, and is quoted as a fixed price per phase after a paid Fit Check. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost.

What does a full Dynamics 365 implementation include?

A full implementation covers everything in your signed scope: configuration of Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service or both, data moved from your current CRM or spreadsheets, the integrations you name, training and go-live. Anything not named in the scope, agents and Microsoft licenses are not part of it.

Included

  • A written scope from a paid Fit Check, with assumptions and exclusions
  • Configuration of Sales, and Customer Service if in scope
  • Data migration from your current CRM or spreadsheets
  • Integrations named in the scope
  • Your Microsoft licenses assigned to each user
  • Training, go-live and handover to a support plan

Not included

  • Anything not named in the signed scope
  • Agents and Copilot Studio work, scoped separately
  • Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts.

Want to know what your project would take?Book a call to scope it

What is the paid Fit Check?

The Fit Check is the paid first step of every full implementation: we review your current system and needs, then give you a written scope and a fixed quote for the build. The quote is yours to keep, whether or not you build with us.

01 · ReviewYour system and needsA review of your current system or need, using our written discovery questionnaire.
02 · ScopeA written scopeA written scope with assumptions, your responsibilities and what is out of scope.
03 · QuoteA fixed quoteA fixed quote for the build, priced per phase.

Fit Check price: quoted in writing. [Brian sets: whether it is credited against the build, and within how many days].

Is a full implementation right for your business?

A full implementation fits a business that needs other systems connected, or data moved from several systems, when Dynamics 365 goes live. It is more than you need if this is your first Dynamics 365 Sales or Customer Service system and your process is standard; an accelerator fits that better.

Not sure? Book a call and we will tell you which package fits.

Book a call

A good fit if

  • You need other systems connected to Dynamics 365 on day one.
  • Your data lives in several systems and has to move at go-live.
  • You want Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service built together.

Consider another option if

  • This is your first Dynamics 365 Sales system and your sales process is standard. The Sales Accelerator is built for that.
  • You already have a Dynamics 365 Sales system that is over-customized or stalled. Rescue and Repair is built for that.
  • You have one or two people who only need a shared address book.

How does a full Dynamics 365 implementation run?

Every project runs through the same four stages: Plan, Build, Go live and Run. You see the written plan before we build, and every change after that is written down and approved.

Stage APlanWe learn how you sell, serve and bill, using a written discovery questionnaire, and give you the plan: apps, users, data, and where Copilot fits.
Stage BBuildWe build Dynamics 365 to the plan, using standard features first, and move your data. You check the imported records against your old system before sign-off.
Stage CGo liveTraining and cut-over day. Copilot is switched on if your plan includes it; agents are scoped separately.
Stage DRunYour support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed.
Our four stages and Microsoft's phases
Our stageMicrosoft's Success by Design phaseWhat happens
Fit Check and Stage A. PlanDiscover and InitiateRequirements, high-level design, written scope and plan
Stage B. BuildImplementBuild to the plan, data moved and checked, integrations
Stage C. Go livePrepareTesting, training, cut-over plan, go-live
Stage D. RunOperateLive system, support plan, next-phase changes

Microsoft's Success by Design framework uses these five phases for Dynamics 365 projects. Microsoft says the framework does not guarantee outcomes; it is a way to catch risks early.

Support starts at $500 a month for 4 hours on the Stability plan, which is the minimum plan for new clients. Larger teams choose Optimization at $1,500 a month for 20 hours or Partnership from $2,000 a month for 35 hours.

Monthly plans run on a 12-month agreement. New clients pay an onboarding fee of up to one month's charge. Hours 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, which means a person has picked up your request, not that it is solved. Every monthly plan includes Microsoft escalation management.

Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.

How long does a Dynamics 365 implementation take?

A full implementation typically takes 8 to 16 weeks, and every project is quoted in writing. You get the plan, with dates, before we build. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less.

What is the difference between an accelerator and a full implementation?

Start from where your system is today: a first Dynamics 365 Sales or Customer Service system fits an accelerator, and a system that needs integrations or data from several systems on day one fits a full implementation. A Dynamics 365 system that is over-customized or stalled fits Rescue and Repair.

What is the paid Fit Check?

The Fit Check is the paid first step of every full implementation: we review your current system and needs, then give you a written scope and a fixed quote for the build. The quote is yours to keep, whether or not you build with us.

Can you move our data from Salesforce, HubSpot or spreadsheets?

Yes. Moving data from your old CRM or spreadsheets is part of a full implementation, and the integrations you name are part of the written scope and its fixed price per phase.

Are Microsoft licenses included?

No. Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits are not part of the package price, and you pay for them separately. As part of the build we assign your licenses to each user and set their security roles, because Microsoft does not let a user open the app until both are done.

What if our scope changes during the project?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. Each phase has its own fixed price, so you approve the cost of a change before it is built.

What are the phases of a Dynamics 365 implementation?

Microsoft's Success by Design framework uses five phases: Discover, Initiate, Implement, Prepare and Operate. Our four stages, Plan, Build, Go live and Run, follow the same path, starting with a written scope from the Fit Check.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.

Are Microsoft licenses included?

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales and the basic Sales agent in Outlook and Teams are included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. Premium Sales agent features need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.

What if we need more than the package covers?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. Integrations and data from other systems are quoted inside the full implementation.

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.
